chapters.title: Rebirth
chapters.content:
The eastern sky was about to break, and the morning breeze carrying the chill of early spring pressed against her face.

Zhengyuan Street was dead silent. The bluestone pavement cast a cold sheen, with only a few sparse breakfast stalls propped up in the hazy dawn light. Low, weary yawns drifted through the air, and even the vermilion gates of the official residences closest to the imperial palace were tightly shut.

Amidst this oppressive stillness, a team of sedan-chair bearers carried two soft sedans, moving with hurried footsteps. Their thick-soled coarse cloth shoes stepped onto the stone slabs without making a single sound.

The pink soft sedan swayed slightly, the tassels on the curtains tracing gentle arcs. The figure inside was indistinct, yet just a glimpse of a profile looked bewitching and full of life.

The entourage stopped in front of a tall and magnificent mansion. The vermilion gates were tightly shut, but no one stepped forward to touch the bronze beast-head knockers on the door; they merely waited quietly to the side, as if trying to blend into the dim dawn light.

The edge of the sky gradually turned the color of a fish belly.

Before long, a page-boy poked his head out from the side door next to the stone lions and welcomed the group inside.

All of this happened silently. Even the page-boy who opened the door kept his head lowered, not daring to speak, fearing that any noise would draw attention.

For no other reason than the fact that the person inside the sedan was none other than a concubine brought into the Crown Prince's mansion from the song-and-dance troupe.

The reigning Crown Prince, Ruan Mingyan, was born of the Empress and was the eldest son. From a youthful age, Emperor Anjing kept him by his side to be taught. Now twenty years old, he was both scholarly and martial, excelled in horseback riding and archery, and possessed outstanding political insights. The ministers in court showered him with praise, and ever since he was named heir apparent, he had been even more diligent, never once showing any act of disobedience.

Such an upright and honorable gentleman had not yet decided on a marriage, nor were there any concubines or bed-chamber maids in his residence. He could truly be described as an ideal match for the noble daughters of the capital. Who knew how many nobles and ministers wanted to marry their daughters into the East Palace to climb up this branch, hoping for glory and prosperity for their clan?

Yet it was precisely this steady, prudent Crown Prince, upon whom such high hopes were pinned, who had now taken in two concubines before marrying a primary wife, and what is more, women hailing from such a place. If word of this were to spread, it would likely damage the Crown Prince's reputation, and the political winds at court would shift accordingly.

Therefore, this matter was handled with the utmost secrecy, and everyone in the Crown Prince's mansion walked on eggshells, terrified that those with ulterior motives would make a fuss over it and criticize the Crown Prince for a lapse in virtue.

The soft sedan entered the mansion and headed straight for the inner courtyard. Even the guards, maidservants, and page-boys on duty in the courtyards had long since received orders and been reassigned.

The massive mansion was shrouded in deep quietude.

Suddenly, the agonizing sensation of the bones in her neck being violently snapped struck her. A horrifying feeling of suffocation made her instinctively flail about like a drowning person, and overwhelming panic filled her chest.

Inside the sedan, Yuan Qiao opened her eyes in a panic, cold sweat having soaked through her undergarments at some unknown point.

With one hand, she clutched tightly at her neck, while the other gripped a silk handkerchief. She gasped heavily for air, recalling the terrifying sensation with a pounding heart. Everything felt like a dream.

Yet that horrifying, intense pain was so vivid it made her whole body tremble. The agony of drawing her last breath in her past life clung to her like the marrow-eating worms, binding her tightly, as if three feet of white silk were still wound around her neck, leaving her unable to draw breath.

The sedan she sat in rocked slightly. For a moment, Yuan Qiao was somewhat confused about her current situation. Everything spun, and she felt dizzy, making it nearly impossible to distinguish between reality and a dream.

Just as the sedan was set down, she lost her balance and bumped into the wooden crossbar inside the sedan cabin, a dull pain immediately shooting across her right shoulder. The genuine pain acted like a blow to the head, finally snapping her muddled brain into a degree of clarity.

Yuan Qiao took a deep breath, steadied herself, and ruthlessly pinched her own arm, finally forcing herself to calm down. She tidied her appearance and looked around.

Pink met her eyes everywhere. Judging by the circumstances, she was most likely inside a sedan chair, and she herself was even dressed in light pink bridal garments.

A multitude of doubts instantly welled up in Yuan Qiao's heart.

What is going on?

Where is she?

Looking closer, the bridal garments embroidered with pink crabapple blossoms were simple in style, yet the fabric was of top quality, and the embroidery technique was superb. The more Yuan Qiao looked, the more familiar it felt, though for a moment she couldn't quite place it.

"Second Madams, please alight from the sedan."

Just as she was puzzled and perplexed, a somewhat stern female voice rang out. A maidservant lifted the sedan curtain, lowered her head slightly, and respectfully extended a hand toward her.

Yuan Qiao could only temporarily set all her thoughts aside, barely steadying her state of mind, and stepped out of the sedan with the maid's assistance.

She would wait and see what on earth was going on before deciding.

With her feet on solid ground, a sense of reality finally returned to Yuan Qiao's heart, and her tense nerves relaxed slightly.

"This maid is called Qingdai. From now on, this maid will attend to Madam." Once Yuan Qiao stood firm, Qingdai curtsied to her, her voice bright and clear.

Following the sound, she saw a little maid of about seventeen or eighteen years old, dressed in a light green narrow-sleeved robe with her hair tied in double buns. Her eyes were bright, and the soft flesh on her cheeks puffed out slightly, giving her the charming and naive air of a young girl.

This is... Qingdai?

Yuan Qiao fished the name of the person before her out of distant memories, and upon realizing who it was, she couldn't help but be slightly startled.

Wasn't this her personal maid who used to serve in her courtyard when she first entered the Crown Prince's mansion? If she remembered correctly, Qingdai had been sold and sent out of the mansion by Jiang Qiyun many years ago. What was happening here?

Looking at Qingdai's naive face, Yuan Qiao felt somewhat lost for a moment.

At the same time, the person in the other sedan had also alighted; it was none other than the top courtesan of the song-and-dance troupe, Jiang Qiyun.

Her skin was whiter than snow, her face like a hibiscus flower, her phoenix eyes shifting with watery light, her slender waist willow-like and graceful. Her movements possessed a natural charm, making her stunningly beautiful beyond compare. Although her bridal garments were simple in style, they instead set off her beauty, making her look even more delicate than flowers and arousing pity. Such looks and figure were enough to make all men in this world fall for her, truly living up to her reputation as the top courtesan.

In comparison, the clear and graceful Yuan Qiao standing nearby appeared far less eye-catching.

Jiang Qiyun was also served by a little maid named Peilan, who looked arrogant and indifferent toward the lesser maids, clearly dissatisfied with today's arrangements.

With a turn of her phoenix eyes, aside from the little maid serving her, there was only one slightly older matron leading a few maidservants in the courtyard. This was worlds apart from the scene she had imagined of towering rows of servants and everyone respectfully welcoming her into the mansion. She frowned unhappily.

Yet Jiang Qiyun was blessed with the face of a beauty; even when she openly displayed her displeasure, it looked like a coquettish pout, failing to elicit any aversion and instead making people feel she had been wronged and treated unfairly.

The servants in the mansion lived by reading people's expressions. With no mistress currently in the residence, these two Madams, though only concubines, were not to be underestimated. Should they gain the Crown Prince's favor and rise to become phoenixes upon branches in the future, it was entirely possible.

At this moment, some inevitably compared the two in their hearts, planning to pledge loyalty and curry favor first so that when the others rose to power later, they might reap some benefits.

Comparing the two, the remarkably beautiful Jiang Qiyun clearly looked more likely to win favor.

Noticing the subtle, lingering gazes cast upon her, Jiang Qiyun did not shrink back. Instead, she curved the corners of her lips into a faint smile, instantly unleashing a hundred charms that made it impossible for people to look away.

Someone couldn't help sighing inwardly: with such a beauty, no wonder even the Crown Prince was captivated.

Meanwhile, Yuan Qiao had no heart to think about any of this. She stared blankly at Qingdai's face, then turned her gaze toward the luxurious and grand inner courtyard of the Crown Prince's mansion, her heart hammering like a drum as she remained dazed and unable to snap out of it.

Wasn't this familiar scene precisely the day she first entered the Crown Prince's mansion?

If all this was not a dream, could she actually have... lived again?!

chapters.title: Entering the Mansion
chapters.content:
Seeing Yuan Qiao staring fixedly at the Crown Prince's mansion with a dull expression, Nanny Jing assumed she had never seen such a illustrious family gate before and was momentarily bewitched, a trace of contempt rising in her heart.

She truly was a woman from a song-and-dance troupe, narrow-minded, lowborn, and so utterly worthless. How could she ever be fit to stay by the Crown Prince's side and serve him?

Looking at the other one, although she hadn't lost her composure, she possessed a vixenish face and was the top courtesan of a pleasure quarter. She looked ambitious and far from simple.

Nanny Jing felt a knot of frustration in her chest. She simply couldn't fathom why the Crown Prince, who had always been prudent, had suddenly taken a fancy to two such unpresentable women, leading him to hastily take in concubines before marrying a primary wife, and even causing the Emperor and Empress to fly into a rage, damaging mother-son relations.

The more she thought about it, the more irritated she became. Her face darkened further, and her tone grew even colder and harder: "Will the two Madams please hurry? Do not delay the hour. Follow this maid to inspect your quarters."

Yuan Qiao's thoughts were pulled back by her voice, and she instinctively turned her head. Meeting Nanny Jing's sharp gaze, her heart gave a sudden, startled leap.

The current situation was still unclear, and people who had died in her memories had suddenly come back to life; this was truly somewhat terrifying. Not knowing what to feel at this moment, Yuan Qiao quickly lowered her eyelids to avoid the gaze, deciding to take things one step at a time.

Indeed, everything was just as it had been in her past life. She was assigned to Wangyue Courtyard, while Jiang Qiyun lived in Tingfeng Courtyard.

Nanny Jing instructed a maidservant to hand each of them a booklet, her tone aloof: "Now that the two Madams have entered the mansion, your former habits should be reined in. If the Madams behave themselves and wholeheartedly serve His Highness, there may be a future for you; if you lack a sense of propriety and act willfully, there is naturally no need for this maid to spell out what kind of end awaits you."

Her gaze lingered on Jiang Qiyun for a fraction longer: "His Highness the Crown Prince is destined to inherit the grand throne in the future. I ask that Madam remember her status and conduct herself accordingly."

"These booklets contain the palace rules and regulations revised by the Imperial Household Department. Please ensure you study them thoroughly and keep them engraved in your hearts. The training matrons of the mansion will also guide the two Madams wholeheartedly, so I ask that you do not slack off."

Jiang Qiyun had always been proud and had been pampered in the world of moonlight and flowers; when had she ever suffered such treatment?

Being rebuked to her face by Nanny Jing, her expression instantly turned somewhat unsightly, and a flash of displeasure crossed her eyes, though she quickly suppressed it.

She knew she had just entered the mansion and had yet to secure her footing, whereas Nanny Jing was an old servant of the estate, and her words were entirely within the bounds of propriety with nothing inappropriate about them. She had no choice but to swallow her anger for the time being.

Yuan Qiao flipped casually through the booklet and found that it was indeed identical down to the last detail with what she remembered. Every single palace rule within it was vividly etched in her mind... This truly was not a dream!

Her fingers gently stroked the words she had once copied countless times in the booklet, and a whirlwind of emotions surged in her chest.

Nanny Jing calmly took in the expressions of the two women: one had resentful eyebrows and overweening pride; the other was absent-minded, like a frightened bird.

She sneered inwardly. With such mental fortitude, if placed within the inner palace, they probably wouldn't survive a few days. The Empress's worries were rather unnecessary after all.

"The two Madams should rest first and properly learn the rules tomorrow. This maid takes her leave."

With that, Nanny Jing turned and left, walking with hurried steps as if she didn't want to stay a moment longer.

Led by maidservants, Yuan Qiao and Jiang Qiyun each entered their respective courtyards.

Seeing Yuan Qiao's tightly drawn expression, Qingdai assumed she had been frightened by Nanny Jing, so she whispered words of comfort: "Madam need not be afraid. Nanny Jing may look stern, but she has the kindest heart. Now that the Crown Prince's mansion has no mistress, Nanny Jing is the one the Empress specifically bestowed upon His Highness after the estate was established to look after his daily life and diet. She manages all the affairs within the mansion. Naturally, she has to assert her authority somewhat, otherwise how could she keep such a large estate in line? But Nanny Jing is not a vicious person."

Qingdai had a lively personality and was close to Yuan Qiao in age. Realizing that Yuan Qiao had an easygoing temperament, she chattered on endlessly, wishing she could spill everything about the mansion like beans tumbling from a pot.

Listening to Qingdai's rambling chatter, Yuan Qiao felt a sense of surrealism. When she first entered the Crown Prince's mansion in her past life, Qingdai had also chattered incessantly by her side just like this.

Hearing it again after so many years, it didn't feel as annoying as before; instead, it felt rather endearing.

In Wangyue Courtyard, the servants were already waiting with lowered heads.

Because she was merely a concubine, there were no head matrons or first- and second-rank maids, but Wangyue Courtyard was still provided with four page-boys and six maidservants and matrons to wait upon her.

Yuan Qiao's calm gaze swept over them, taking in those unfamiliar faces, some respectful, some probing.

In her past life, she hadn't even recognized all of these people; once Jiang Qiyun gained favor, the attendants in Wangyue Courtyard were quickly transferred away for various reasons.

Entering the inner chambers, the rough-cleaning maids had already prepared everything necessary for bathing. The pink bridal garments she had changed out of were carefully folded by Qingdai and draped over a clothes rack.

The fabric of the bridal gown was top-tier cloud brocade, which seemed to shimmer with a lustrous sheen upon close inspection, and the embroidered crabapples were lifelike and breathtaking.

Qingdai reached out to stroke the smooth hem, unable to help herself from saying: "According to the regulations, concubines are not permitted to wear bridal garments, yet His Highness the Crown Prince permitted Madam to enter the mansion wearing bridal attire. It is evident that he holds you in high regard!"

These words carried a hint of ingratiation.

Yuan Qiao glanced at them, but a wave of chilliness couldn't help welling up in her heart.

The pale pink color and the ordinary style all too clearly signaled her unpresentable status. No matter how pretty or expensive it was, it was truly difficult to feel any joy toward it.

What was more, this honor was not given to her, but to that phantom who stood in for a dancer at Xuyun Tower and gave him a glimpse that took his breath away. She was merely riding the coattails of "that person." In the end, in his heart, she was just an incidental, inconsequential tag-along.

"Put it away." Yuan Qiao looked away, unwilling to gaze upon it any longer.

The story is not yet finished, please click the next page to continue reading the exciting content!

Inside the bath chamber, swirling steam mixed with the faint fragrance of flower petals, allowing one to relax.

Yuan Qiao stripped off her garments, slowly stepped into the wooden tub, and sank her tired body into the warm water, letting out an almost imperceptible sigh of relief.

Qingdai perceptively stepped forward and placed a soft towel behind Yuan Qiao's neck to prevent the rough edge of the tub from chafing her skin.

Seeing no further instructions, Qingdai quietly retreated behind the screen.

The warm water washed over her skin, warmth gradually rising, and the ice at the bottom of her heart seemed to melt slightly. The bright flower petals floating on the water's surface emitted a faint, delicate fragrance. All of this served as a stark, genuine reminder; she was alive; she had truly come back to life.

Yuan Qiao closed her eyes, trying her utmost to suppress her emotions, but the scenes from her past life rushed over her like a tidal wave.

How difficult was it for a lowborn, powerless concubine to survive within this man-eating Crown Prince's mansion?

Yet back then, mired in the quagmire, she had still clung to that ridiculous sense of pride, leading to step-by-step mistakes that harmed both herself and others.

Recalling everything she had endured, Yuan Qiao felt an unplacable congestion in her chest. No one knew the sorrow and bitterness in her heart, nor did anyone know the pain and despair of being trapped in a cage, watching the people around her leave one by one, until her final desperate struggle proved to be nothing more than futile, ultimately ending in her being strangled to death.

Yuan Qiao had never possessed much ambition. She neither fawned upon power nor condescended to flattery; what she sought was merely a safe and peaceful life. She had never imagined becoming someone above others, able to summon wind and rain one day.

Yet this magnificent and grand Crown Prince's mansion was like a giant beast, continuously devouring the last remnants of her clarity, and like an all-encompassing net, trapping her tightly as she tried to break free, ultimately dragging her into an endless abyss to drown in years devoid of light.

Before her thoughts could settle, the door was gently knocked upon. Following a burst of whispers, Qingdai walked in with brisk footsteps.

"Madam, word has come from the outer courtyard that the morning court session has ended, and His Highness the Crown Prince is about to return to the mansion. We must hurry!"

chapters.title: Dressing to Await His Arrival
chapters.content:
Qingdai spoke with a hint of urgency, "This servant heard that the people over at Tingfeng Courtyard have already finished dressing and are just waiting for His Highness's summons. The servants in this manor are the best at trimming their sails to the wind. Today is your very first day entering the manor; if you are outshone right from the start, our days here will be difficult indeed!"

Seeing that Yuan Qiao's expression held not a trace of panic, Qingdai couldn't help stamping her foot. "If I may be so bold, in this deep courtyard, His Highness's favor is the foundation upon which we make our living. Madam, you must make plans early!"

The Crown Prince. It was always the Crown Prince.

As in her past life, Qingdai was still prompting her at every turn to vie for favor.

For in Qingdai's view, a concubine of humble birth like Yuan Qiao would have nothing but endless bitterness and suffering ahead if she failed to firmly establish her footing before the primary wife entered the manor.

In the past, Yuan Qiao had prided herself on being above worldly things, unwilling to stoop to serving a lord with her looks. She had thought Qingdai, at such a tender age, knew only of scheming and calculating, and had been unwilling to curry favor with the Crown Prince as Qingdai suggested. Instead, she had avoided him at all turns, leading her to an increasingly desperate plight.

Yet, what Qingdai said was not entirely unreasonable.

If she wanted to gain a firm foothold in the Crown Prince's Mansion and avoid being wantonly humiliated, she had to win Ruan Mingyan's favor. Not to mention monopolizing his affections, she at least could not allow Jiang Qiyun to monopolize his grace and drive her step by step into a desperate corner as she had in her past life.

She currently had nothing. Therefore, if she wanted to survive, she had to rely on him, no matter how unwilling she might be.

"No need to say more."

Yuan Qiao rose from the wooden tub. Seeing Qingdai so anxious her face had flushed red, she put down her towel and said calmly, "What is there to rush? Everything must be done step by step."

Although Qingdai harbored her own selfish motives, what she did was ultimately so the two of them could live a little better in the manor. Now that Yuan Qiao had seen through things, she no longer felt there was anything wrong with this.

Diligently serving Yuan Qiao as she put on her undergarments, Qingdai fetched a tray upon which rested a neatly folded camellia-red, gold-brocaded, intertwined-lotus-patterned silk tunic. The fabric's luster shifted continuously, exuding magnificent luxury. Yuan Qiao knew at a glance that it was handcrafted from the palace.

Such over-regulated, precious items appearing in the quarters of a mere concubine, rather than a reward, it was more like a probe, a careless reprimand from those in power.

This also meant that whenever the slightest disturbance occurred in this residence, it could not escape the eyes of the person in the palace.

On the dressing table sat another wooden tray, holding a set of gold-inlaid ruby head ornaments. The rubies were of exceptional quality, and the workmanship was extremely refined.

Both the garments and the jewelry were of immeasurable value.

Yuan Qiao's gaze swept over that glaring patch of red, much like sweeping over the bloody tears that had swallowed her up in her past life.

Her fingertips trembled imperceptibly, and her hands, curled within her sleeves, tightened instinctively, yet her expression remained as still as stagnant water. "Too garish. Change into something plain."

Looking at Yuan Qiao's fair and pretty yet somewhat pale face, Qingdai couldn't help offering a few more words: "Madam, this set of camellia-red, gold-brocaded intertwined-lotus silk tunic complements your complexion best..."

Unwilling to say more, Yuan Qiao simply stated, "Change into something else."

Having floated and sunk in the deep palace for over a decade in her past life, even though she had never attained a high rank, she would truly have lived her past life in vain if she couldn't even see through such a superficial ploy.

Besides, she was unsuited for such gaudy colors to begin with.

Jiang Qiyun possessed a striking and vibrant beauty; if she wore bright colors, she would only appear more alluring and charming. But if Yuan Qiao were to wear this outfit to see Ruan Mingyan, it would border on looking like Dong Shi mimicking Xi Shi (trying to imitate beauty and making a fool of oneself).

Since she had resolved to vie for favor, she naturally had to put some thought into it.

In the end, Yuan Qiao chose a silver-white moon-flower skirt embroidered with broken-branch florals, paired with a light-blue pearled-teardrop tassel wrap. For jewelry, she picked a matching set of silver and jade hair ornaments, simple and elegant.

The reflection in the mirror was fresh and refined; though she applied only the lightest touch of cosmetics, it did not appear drab.

If Jiang Qiyun was a dazzling and eye-catching peony that caused a hundred flowers to lose their luster and fade into obscurity the moment she appeared, then Yuan Qiao was a cold camellia, not abrupt, not glaring, yet strikingly ethereal and possessing a unique charm of her own.

Qingdai smoothed out the creases of the silk wrap and praised, "Madam is born so lovely and possesses such an extraordinary disposition, you will surely make His Highness the Crown Prince look upon you with new eyes."

Yuan Qiao was noncommittal regarding these remarks.

When it came to appearance alone, very few in the capital could compare to Jiang Qiyun's beauty. Which man would not be moved by such an absolute stunner? Even Ruan Mingyan had fallen for her at first sight, disregarding his reputation to take her as a concubine before even marrying a primary wife, how utterly absurd.

Yuan Qiao smoothed her sleeves and sat leisurely before the table, instructing Qingdai to fetch some food.

Having been fussed over since the fourth watch, she had not yet had a single drop of water or grain of rice, and her stomach was already completely empty. No matter what she planned to do next, she had to appease her own mortal frame first.

Having received her orders and assuming they were prepared for the Crown Prince, Qingdai hurried the servants below to arrange it.

Before long, plates of delicate pastries were brought over, along with a pot of fine Spring Mountain Oolong tea.

Qingdai happily said, "This tea is what His Highness the Crown Prince usually drinks. Later, when Madam offers tea to His Highness and whispers a few sweet words, you will surely be able to keep him..."

Before she finished speaking, she saw Yuan Qiao pick up a piece of cloud-slice pastry, take a bite, and chew it slowly, even pouring a cup of tea to accompany it. The rest of her words instantly stuck in her throat.

"Madam, you..."

Qingdai hesitated, stopping and starting, until finally she let out a soft sigh and stood quietly to one side.

So be it; she was, after all, the mistress.

Yuan Qiao took another bite of the pastry. The mild sweetness of the cloud-slice pastry paired with the fragrance of the tea was just the right combination.

Naturally, she knew what Qingdai was worrying about.

In her past life, the moment Ruan Mingyan returned to the mansion, he went straight to Jiang Qiyun's quarters, only later glancing briefly at Wangyue Courtyard. At that time, she had no heart to vie for favor and naturally couldn't offer him any pleasant expressions, so Ruan Mingyan left without even sitting down.

She had just entered the mansion now. Even if she knew what would happen, she could not proactively crowd around Ruan Mingyan. After all, there were the Empress's eyes and ears in this manor; jumping around recklessly now, was she wishing she would die any faster?

It would be better to wait and watch the changes, then slowly plot her course after Ruan Mingyan arrived.

In her past life, ever since entering the mansion, Jiang Qiyun indulged in nightly favors, repeatedly making things difficult for Mama Jing and clashing with the etiquette instructors. Within a few days, an imperial edict summoned her into the palace to study decorum for half a month. When she returned to the manor, she was thoroughly haggard, like a flower beaten by frost, and it took her several months to recover. One could easily imagine how much torment she had suffered in the palace.

This also showed that sticking out and showing off one's sharpness was absolutely unacceptable; the person in the palace would not tolerate it.

Thinking of this, Yuan Qiao picked up another piece of osmanthus cake and shoved it into her mouth.

The osmanthus cake was powdery, soft, and sweet, but a bit dry. Just as she was about to ask Qingdai to check the kitchen for some soup or other throat-friendly food, she suddenly saw a figure silently appear at the doorway and was instantly startled.

The person appeared abruptly against the backlight. At first glance, the figure was tall and slender, and only after he stepped into the room did Yuan Qiao fully see his face.

It was Ruan Mingyan.

The osmanthus cake was not small, and Yuan Qiao had been exceedingly hungry, swallowing a piece whole just moments before. At that moment, suddenly seeing Ruan Mingyan was no different from seeing a ghost. In her sudden agitation, the crumbly, dry pastry fragments clogged her windpipe, nearly choking her to death.

Aside, Qingdai had already knelt down in a panic and joy, just as she was about to softly remind Yuan Qiao to pay her respects, she saw Yuan Qiao's face turn crimson, coughing uncontrollably, causing Qingdai's vision to go dark.

What kind of mess was this!

Ruan Mingyan had not yet changed out of his court robes. The wide and solemn court attire, with its white base and red lining, was embroidered with the Chi dragon patterns representing his status in gold thread. A black-and-red leather belt was tightly bound around his waist, dangling a gilded beast-head pendant.

This outfit alone was intimidating enough, yet at the moment his gaze was fixed heavily on Yuan Qiao, making Qingdai's heart beat like a war drum and her hands and feet feel as though they had been nailed to the floor in helpless confusion.

Ruan Mingyan swept a cold glance at Qingdai, his voice as clear as a spring, "What are you standing there stunned for? Hurry up and pour tea for your mistress."

Only then did Qingdai snap out of her daze, rushing forward to pour tea for Yuan Qiao and gently patting her back to help her catch her breath.

Once she recovered, the mistress and servant knelt down toward Ruan Mingyan together, bowing their heads low like quails.

Yuan Qiao was astonished by Ruan Mingyan's sudden arrival, yet also felt embarrassed and ashamed by her loss of composure just now. At the same time, the entanglement and resentment of her past life were stirred up once more, leaving her temporarily at a loss as to how to face the person before her. Thus, she simply lowered her head, refusing to look at Ruan Mingyan, and her voice remained somewhat hoarse as she offered the greeting, "Greetings, Your Highness the Crown Prince."

"Lift your head."

Yuan Qiao paused, remaining motionless for a moment.

Ruan Mingyan's expression was bland, revealing neither joy nor anger, as he simply repeated: "Lift it."

chapters.title: Loss of Composure
chapters.content:
Yuan Qiao was somewhat bewildered. She raised her head as told, but her gaze remained lowered, avoiding Ruan Mingyan's line of sight.

In her past life, after Ruan Mingyan ascended the throne, his majesty grew day by day. Though Yuan Qiao also entered the palace, she never enjoyed imperial favor. She usually lived alone in a remote courtyard, left unattended even during the empress's daily morning assemblies, as if no one cared whether she showed up or whether she was dead or alive.

The few times they met, you could count them on one hand, were during grand palace banquets. Even then, she had merely followed protocol by lowering her head to pay respects; how could she ever dare to look the Son of Heaven directly in the face?

Seeing him now once more, regardless of how her thoughts churned within, her body seemed to have remembered the terror of old first, dragging up a measure of timidity.

Because of the earlier coughing fit, the young woman's fair face was still tinted with a light flush, and the corners of her eyes were brushed with pink. Her lowered, phoenix-like eyes held rippling moisture, adding a pitiful, heart-touching quality to her appearance. Her simple dress and delicate makeup only served to highlight her pure and graceful features, making her look like a freshly blooming lotus, fresh, refined, and demure.

As Ruan Mingyan looked at her, he felt a certain spot in his heart soften, involuntarily stirred to a trace of pity.

Suddenly, his gaze paused, landing on the corner of her lips, a few crumbs of pastry still remained there.

Recalling the young woman's panic-stricken appearance when she first saw him, Ruan Mingyan couldn't help frowning slightly, his dark gaze tinged with a hint of displeasure.

Whether it sprang from her fear of him or something else, he could not tell.

"Rise," he said, his tone flat, revealing neither happiness nor anger. "Since you have entered the manor, your words and actions must be dignified from now on."

With those words, Ruan Mingyan stood up and left, not staying for even half a moment more.

Seeing Ruan Mingyan's figure disappear beyond the moon gate, Yuan Qiao let out a sigh of relief. As if having survived a catastrophe, she allowed Qingdai to support her as she slowly sat back down at the table.

"Madam," Qingdai said, her face pale with lingering fear as she watched Yuan Qiao, hesitating, "Could it be that His Highness the Crown Prince is displeased?"

Yuan Qiao shook her head.

In her past life, she lacked the Emperor's favor and remained a mere Zhaoyi until her death purely on the grounds of being an old acquaintance from the Prince's estate. In the palace, she could barely manage to preserve her own life, ultimately unable to truly fathom the fathomless depths of the ruler's heart. Yet even so, she understood that losing her composure just now was a fact; had anyone else witnessed it, even Ruan Mingyan would have lost face along with her.

After all, she had entered the Crown Prince's Mansion now, and every action tied into the household's reputation. It was only natural that he would be displeased.

Moreover...

Yuan Qiao lowered her gaze to look at her flat abdomen. Even though nothing had happened yet, she still could not let go entirely.

Yuan Qiao sighed. "So be it. I suppose I simply don't have the fate to be a favored concubine. I even have to learn the skills of bowing low and pleasing others."

She was never one to bend her personality to flatter others. If she forcibly relied on such tactics to vie for favor, it would likely backfire. Her initial setback today perhaps signaled that this path would be rugged and difficult to tread.

After all, she could not let go of the past, could not forget the old affections, nor could she forgive the one from the past.

Yuan Qiao was someone who had died once already and was quite broad-minded. After reflecting upon it for a moment, she looked at the culprit on the table, drew a painful lesson from the experience, and ordered, "Go to the kitchen and see if there is any soup or broth. These pastries look nice, but they truly choke you."

Hearing this, Qingdai wore a complex expression. She almost admired her mistress; the Crown Prince had flicked his sleeves and left, yet instead of thinking about how to win him back, Madam could still eat?

These plates of pastries were exquisitely made, and even the arrangement and color coordination took considerable effort. Normally, they were exclusively reserved for the Crown Prince's enjoyment. Today, having failed to gain favor, she feared Madam wouldn't even get to eat them in the future.

With a drooping face, Qingdai trudged toward the kitchen with heavy steps, as if she could already foresee their bleak days ahead.

Seeing her like this, Yuan Qiao couldn't help smiling.

The young girl had shallow thoughts; her joys and sorrows were plainly hung on her face, making her far more endearing than those honey-mouthed, sword-hearted individuals.

Things had only just begun. If she were to eagerly vie for favor, it would only appear deliberate. As long as she wasn't as foolish as in her past life, she naturally wouldn't fall into such a miserable plight.

Before long, Qingdai returned from the kitchen holding a freshly stewed bowl of red date and bird's nest soup, followed by another maid who had gone out to gather news.

The news was that the Crown Prince had lingered at Tingfeng Courtyard for a long time, and his midday meal had also been served there.

Yuan Qiao paused, then quickly returned to normal.

Ruan Mingyan had taken a fancy to Jiang Qiyun in the first place, which was why today's events unfolded as they did. Not to mention sharing a meal, he would likely stay the night there as well. Since she already knew this from her past life, why torment herself by dwelling on it now?

Take it slow, Yuan Qiao comforted herself. Vying for favor was inferior to fighting for survival; steady progress and solid steps were the only way for the long term.

Even if she failed to win his affection, as long as she showed her face before Ruan Mingyan more often, constantly expressing care and admiration so he wouldn't forget she existed, and securing a higher rank in the future to avoid being inexplicably murdered; that would be enough.

Ever since hearing the news, Qingdai had grown secretly anxious. Seeing that Yuan Qiao seemed indifferent, she became even more restless, pacing like an ant on a hot pan and asking repeatedly, "Madam, what should we do?"

"What is there to rush?"

Yuan Qiao glanced at Qingdai, her tone still calm. "The days ahead are long. Flowers do not bloom for a hundred days, and people do not stay prosperous forever. The days are still long, so just take it one step at a time."

For a short while, Jiang Qiyun would not be lording it over her head; the shrewd people in this manor would at least wait until Jiang Qiyun completely crushed her into a position of no return before kicking her while she was down.

And she was no longer the person who allowed herself to be bullied at will.

Looking at Yuan Qiao's composed demeanor, Qingdai's thoughts gradually settled. Realizing her own lapse in decorum, she hurriedly said, "This servant lost her composure."

By dusk, news indeed came from Tingfeng Courtyard that the Crown Prince was staying the night.

Since they had entered the manor in the same batch and were simultaneously assigned to serve the newly arrived mistresses, Qingdai inevitably harbored a desire to compare herself with Peilan, though having just been reprimanded by Yuan Qiao, she dared not say much more.

---

Night fell, and a cool breeze stirred.

Yuan Qiao draped an outer robe over her shoulders and sat on the low couch by the window. Outside, the drooping crabapple flower buds were plump, their blossoms hanging like dots of rouge from the branches.

She sipped her tea. Though she was physically and mentally exhausted, she felt not a shred of sleepiness.

The nights in the Crown Prince's Mansion were always so long and desolate, offering no glimpse of dawn. She had endured countless such nights before plunging into the even darker deep palace, ultimately losing her life there.

After turning full circle, she had now returned to this place, hardly a result of anything other than the unpredictable twists of fate.

The moonlight outside the window grew increasingly cold.

The lanterns along the corridor swayed gently in the wind, casting shifting tree shadows that dragged her back to that unbearable night in her past life.

By then, Jiang Qiyun had already been bestowed the title of Crown Prince's Liangyuan, reigning at the height of favor. In the manor, she acted entirely like the mistress of the house, surrounded by numerous followers.

Yet Yuan Qiao's courtyard was desolate in the extreme, with only Qingdai and two rough-cleaning maids left by her side. She often sat alone in the dead of night until dawn, gazing up at the four-square sky, unable to understand why she had been trapped in this cage that was gilded on the outside.

If one spoke of birth, Jiang Qiyun was merely a dancing girl who had sold herself in a song-and-dance house, even lower than a registered commoner's daughter like Yuan Qiao. Yet relying on her alluring bones and schemes, she had risen step by step from a lowly concubine to a Crown Prince's Liangyuan, until no one dared look down upon her.

And what of herself?

They had entered the manor on the very same day, yet their fates were poles apart. In this vast Crown Prince's Mansion, no one cared whether she lived or died. The Crown Prince's neglect, Jiang Qiyun's bullying, and the servants' harsh treatment were like pots of ice water that extinguished the last shred of hope in her heart.

She had never longed for wealth and glory; otherwise, she would have sought a patron early on back in the song-and-dance house. The harsh predicament in the manor filled her with the desire to retreat, and she mustered the greatest courage of her life to kneel and beg the Crown Prince to let her leave the manor, vowing to enter Jing'an Temple to keep company with the green lamps and ancient Buddha, praying for the Crown Prince's blessings.

Who could have expected that the day the Crown Prince returned from a banquet, having apparently consumed quite a bit of wine, his drunkenness led him to mistake her for Jiang Qiyun... After a night of folly, she became pregnant.

Since she had received his favor and was now with child, her plea to leave the manor was naturally denied.

Because of this unexpected child, the Crown Prince finally stopped ignoring her as he had before, occasionally visiting Wangyue Courtyard. Naturally, her days in the manor became somewhat easier.

At the time, she had naively believed this was a lifeline granted to her by fate, thinking perhaps she too could gain a foothold in the Crown Prince's Mansion. But later she realized it was merely fate mocking her.

This Crown Prince's Mansion was never a place that could harbor hope.

Jiang Qiyun had enjoyed the Crown Prince's favor for a long time without conceiving; how could she tolerate someone else bearing a child overnight? Before the first three months had passed, she lost her child due to tainted food. Clearly, Qingdai had inspected all her food one by one, how could such an oversight occur? Not only that, but her family far away in Tang County also met a tragic end, said to have been killed by a disaster. But how could there be such a coincidental disaster? Under the double blow, she was almost driven out of her mind.

The Crown Prince, unaware of the truth, assumed she simply refused to bear his flesh and blood, abandoned her completely, and never favored her again.

The servants in the courtyard scattered, and even Qingdai was cruelly sold off. In the end, Mama Jing couldn't bear to watch and assigned two people to look after her.

Because of the miscarriage, she was left with a lingering illness and could no longer conceive, making her even more hopeless in this manor, living in a daze day after day.

Later, Crown Princess Lian entered the manor, and she and Jiang Qiyun, who had now been promoted to a Secondary Consort, became pregnant one after the other. No one remembered the dispensable person that was Yuan Qiao. Only Jiang Qiyun would occasionally stroll past the gates of Wangyue Courtyard, heavily pregnant, with a smile on her face that was sharper than winter icicles.

Thinking back now, that night had not been a blessing, but rather the genesis of all her sufferings.

In her memory, Ruan Mingyan's appearance completely overlapped with the visage he wore earlier as he looked down upon her from his lofty height.

Yuan Qiao tightened her grip on her cup and drained the tea in a single gulp. The thoroughly chilled tea carried a biting coldness that instantly spread through her limbs and bones, chilling even the tip of her heart.

Yet within her eyes, the previous confusion and timidity were gone, replaced solely by a cold light as still and deep as water.

chapters.title: Learning Etiquette
chapters.content:
The following day, according to the customs for concubines entering the estate, Yuan Qiao and Jiang Qiyun should have gone to present tea to the mistress of the house. However, with the position of Crown Princess currently vacant, this ritual was omitted as well.

The Listening Wind Courtyard had received rewards early in the morning. Though it was not broadcasted widely, it was enough to make the servants of the estate quietly weigh their options. Everyone held their breath and watched these two newly arrived madams, none daring to place their bets easily.

Just past the hour of Chen (7:00 to 9:00 AM), a maid came over to pass along a message, saying that Mama Jing and the training matrons were already waiting at the Orchid Verdant Pavilion and requested Yuan Qiao to come over.

In her past life, Yuan Qiao had suffered no small amount of hardship learning these rules.

She came from the countryside, having lost her father at a young age, and was raised by her aunt. Later, by a stroke of fortune, she met a dancer and learned a few skills, finally earning a living in a song-and-dance house. A few taels of silver a month was already immense security to her.

The capital was as prosperous as brocade, yet she could scarcely catch a glimpse of it, let alone ever touch the rigorous courtyard training of such a noble family.

Had it not been for dancing in Jiang Qiyun's stead that day and catching the Crown Prince's eye all at once, she would likely have been like the other women in the workshop, saving up enough silver to retire to the countryside and live out her days in obscurity.

Outside people all said she had climbed a high branch and was blessed with fortunes cultivated over several lifetimes, yet no one knew that those stern palace rules had once nearly crushed half her life out of her.

Thinking back on it now, it felt almost like a dream.

Yuan Qiao let out a soft breath and, leaning on Qingdai's hand, headed toward the Orchid Verdant Pavilion.

The pavilion was not far from the main courtyard, connected by winding corridors and layered artificial mountains dotted with vibrant greenery. Under the eaves were planted many rare varieties of orchids, emitting a secluded and graceful posture, showing they were tended by dedicated hands.

Yuan Qiao had never paid attention to these things before; now that she saw them, she couldn't help taking a few extra glances, her pace slowing down as well.

"You've arrived quite early."

A charming voice came from behind.

Yuan Qiao turned back to look and saw Jiang Qiyun, leaning on Peilan's hand, walking slowly toward this side.

Today, she wore a cloud-satin dress embroidered with a hundred butterflies weaving through flowers, her raven hair coiled into an intricate bun adorned with an expensive set of head ornaments. She was gorgeously adorned and breathtakingly beautiful, quite eye-catching.

Unwilling to pick a fight with her, Yuan Qiao paused and stood aside to let Jiang Qiyun go first.

Seeing her so tactful, Jiang Qiyun hooked the corners of her lips, revealing a trace of complacency. "Come to think of it, your ability to enter the Crown Prince's mansion is entirely thanks to my favorable wind. Remember to always keep my kindness in mind from now on."

As the two brushed past each other, Jiang Qiyun lowered her voice as if in warning, "Remember to conduct yourself properly and not covet things that do not belong to you."

Knowing that Jiang Qiyun was deliberately trying to make things unpleasant for her, Yuan Qiao merely lowered her gaze and remained silent, her eyes calm and unruffled.

She was not in a hurry to do anything. After all, the grudges of her past life were as deep as the sea; there was no need to rush for a momentary sense of satisfaction. Now, seeing this "old acquaintance" again, she instead birthed a few other amusing thoughts.

Seeing her unmoved, Jiang Qiyun curled her lip, finding it utterly boring. With a cold snort, she walked straight into the room.

"Madam, she is simply too bullying!" Qingdai couldn't help muttering, feeling aggrieved on behalf of her own mistress.

"It's fine." Yuan Qiao looked at the gorgeous retreating figure, a trace of an extremely faint curve escaping the corners of her lips.

Making a scene right at the entrance of the pavilion, was this out of fear that the people inside wouldn't know?

Come to think of it, in her previous life, Jiang Qiyun had never taken her seriously either, becoming even worse after gaining favor. If not for Mama Jing suppressing things in the estate, there was no telling how much mischief Jiang Qiyun would have stirred up.

In this lifetime, she would never let herself fall into that kind of state again.

She would take it all back.

---

The Orchid Verdant Pavilion had an incense burner placed inside. The bluish smoke of Zeyuan incense rose in spirals, drifting out past the window lattices, rendered misty and hazy by the morning sun.

The training matron and Mama Jing sat in the seats of honor.

Both were female officials who had come out of the palace and held official ranks. Even when serving in the Crown Prince's mansion, they were different from ordinary maidservants, wearing female official uniforms and carrying an air of natural authority that brooked no disrespect.

Seeing Yuan Qiao and Jiang Qiyun enter, the two did not stand, merely giving slight nods to acknowledge their bow.

Sweeping her gaze across them, Mama Jing understood clearly in her heart.

Compared to yesterday, this Madam Yuan looked much more appropriate; her expression was calm and restrained, and her attire was also plain. Madam Jiang, on the other hand, was increasingly flamboyant, dressed in luxurious garments with her temples full of pearls and jade, while her brows and the corners of her eyes could not conceal her arrogance.

Having won favor for merely a night and she is already this conceited and carried away?

Mama Jing frowned fiercely and said in a deep voice, "Did the two madams read that booklet yesterday?"

Her voice was not loud, yet it carried unquestionable dignity.

Yuan Qiao slightly lowered her head and replied softly, "Replying to Mama, I have read it carefully." Her posture was submissive, without any fault.

Mama Jing nodded, her gaze falling upon Jiang Qiyun.

A trace of panic flashed across the depths of Jiang Qiyun's eyes. Yesterday she had been solely preoccupied with joy, how could she remember any booklet of palace rules? However, that trace of panic was quickly replaced by disdain; she didn't think this was a big deal, even believing that the old hag before her was deliberately making things difficult for her.

Seeing Jiang Qiyun's reaction, without needing to ask further, it was obvious she hadn't taken it to heart at all. Mama Jing said no more, turning to say to the training matron, "The two madams have just entered the estate and many rules are still unknown to them. I must trouble the matron to put in more effort."

The training matron naturally understood Mama Jing's meaning.

People who came out of the palace had plenty of methods at their disposal, let alone teaching etiquette; even if it was somewhat strict, no fault could be found.

The thick sandalwood ruler looked ordinary, leaving not the slightest trace when it struck the body, yet it hurt fiercely.

In barely two hours, Jiang Qiyun had lost all color in her face, struggling even to stand. The arrogant momentum she came with was completely gone, and even that pile of luxurious hair ornaments on her head had become a burden. However haughty and arrogant she had been upon arrival, she was just as wretched now.

The training matron watched with cold eyes, showing not a shred of pity, "Madam Jiang still needs to practice diligently after returning. Tomorrow, this old slave will inspect again."

In comparison, Yuan Qiao fared much better.

She already knew these rules by heart, though she didn't display perfection everywhere on the very first day to arouse suspicion. Instead, she wholeheartedly "learned," slowly improving step by step. By half a day's time, she was already doing quite decently, naturally avoiding any punishment. When leaving, she even bid farewell to the training matron and Mama Jing almost impeccably.

The mistress and servant strolled slowly along the corridor toward the Watching Moon Courtyard. Compared to Jiang Qiyun, their return could be described as leisurely.

Recalling Jiang Qiyun's forced composure upon leaving, Qingdai felt deeply vindicated, almost unable to suppress her smile.

Both were concubines, as if one was loftier than the other, making things difficult for her mistress early in the morning, serving her right!

Once they returned to the courtyard, Qingdai finally poured out all the words she had bottled up along the way like peas spilling from a pod: "Did Madam see? When Madam Jiang came out, her face was completely white! Serving her right for being a gossipy busybody early in the morning and asking for trouble, she deserved to be taught a lesson. Still, our Madam is amazing, learning the rules so well! This maid used to be terribly slow at learning rules and was scolded by the managing mamas quite a few times."

Maids entering the estate also had to be thoroughly disciplined before serving their masters. Moreover, this was the Crown Prince's mansion, where all rules followed those of the palace and were even more rigorous. Qingdai and Peilan had naturally gone through such an ordeal themselves.

However, the rules for mistresses were somewhat different. Now that Yuan Qiao and Jiang Qiyun were following the lessons on palace rules, the maids merely observed from the side and did not need to practice along.

Yet what Yuan Qiao thought of ran deeper: although the training matron and Mama Jing were both palace veterans, why was she so severe with Jiang Qiyun today solely based on Mama Jing's instruction? The so-called negligence of rules was merely a pretext; behind this, there was likely the tacit permission of someone with even higher status.

"Alright," seeing Qingdai beaming with excitement, Yuan Qiao reminded, "Do not get carried away."

Qingdai hastily nodded and shifted the topic elsewhere.

---

Matters within the estate naturally could not be hidden from Ruan Mingyan's ears; even the confrontation in the corridor was reported to him word for word.

Inside the study, Ruan Mingyan listened to the report while his fingertips stroked a purple-jade wolf-hair brush.

He recalled the day he entered the Watching Moon Courtyard, when Yuan Qiao had looked at him blankly, her gaze clear and her courage small. Just being glanced at by him had scared her like that, making her pitiful indeed. Now that she had been bullied, she didn't dare utter even half a word, which showed she was being suppressed everywhere in the estate.

So be it; after all, it was he who had dragged her into this. If he didn't protect her a little and she was truly bullied harshly, she would probably hide away to cry in secret, not even daring to complain.

Ruan Mingyan thus instructed: "Lunch will be served at the Watching Moon Courtyard."

chapters.title: Sharing Lunch
chapters.content:
When the news reached the Watching Moon Courtyard, Yuan Qiao was just about to take a nap.

Having slept poorly last night, going early in the morning to learn etiquette, tossing about through a round of it, and then having to deal with two sharp-eyed matrons without making a single mistake, all of this had consumed nearly half of Yuan Qiao's mental energy. At that moment, she only felt a heavy wave of drowsiness and intended to make do with a hasty lunch.

Who would have thought that a page from the outer courtyard would suddenly send word that the Crown Prince was coming to the Watching Moon Courtyard for lunch? This meant she could no longer be perfunctory.

Yuan Qiao had no choice but to forcefully gather away her weariness, re-do her hair and makeup, and prepare to serve the Crown Prince's meal.

Regarding this, Yuan Qiao felt no great joy in her heart.

She knew very well who Ruan Mingyan currently favored more. She might have merely stirred up a bit of the pity that he, as a superior, held for a weak dependent, or perhaps he was simply sharing his favors impartially, but this was far from enough.

However, in her past life, Ruan Mingyan had not set foot in the Watching Moon Courtyard at this time.

This tiny difference, like a pebble tossed into dead water, sent ripples spreading outward. A trace of extremely faint light seemed to pierce through the depths of her dormant heart, making her even firmer in her path forward.

Qingdai, on the other hand, was immensely happy, feeling that this was the arrival of her mistress's favor. She personally ran to the kitchens to keep an eye on the dishes and instructed others to arrange the dining table, busy to the point of running off her feet. Seeing her joy, Yuan Qiao let her be.

When Ruan Mingyan arrived, he still did not have anyone announce him, as if disliking having people shout out his presence everywhere, and walked straight into the courtyard.

Fortunately, having learned her lesson from last time, Qingdai had kept her eye on the movement at the doorway and reminded Yuan Qiao early on, so the mistress and servant did not repeat past mistakes.

"No need for formalities."

Ruan Mingyan's voice was flat. Entering the room, seeing some pre-meal tea snacks and appetizer plates set out on the table, he assumed Yuan Qiao was hungry. Figuring that she had struggled through half a day and was indeed exhausted, he instructed, "Serve the meal."

Seeing his cold expression, as if he had truly come solely for the sake of eating and had no mood for idle chatter, Yuan Qiao pursed her lips. The soft words she had brewed for a long time were silently swallowed back, and she could only inwardly sigh that she truly wasn't cut out for this.

However, she was not willing to fawn over him or curry favor either.

The lunch was extremely lavish, prepared entirely according to the standards of the Crown Prince's ordinary meals: cold dishes, stir-fries, soups, pastries, and fruit platters, altogether a hundred-odd varieties, spread out in a dazzling array.

Not only was the table packed full, but several dining eunuchs holding food trays also stood quietly at the side to serve.

Qingdai had previously done chores like sweeping and cleaning and had never served in the main courtyard, so she was inevitably a bit flustered facing this kind of scene.

Yuan Qiao, however, had witnessed the grand scale of palace banquets; the current display could not move her. It was just that she had no appetite today, and after taking a few bites of plain seasonal vegetables, she wanted to set down her chopsticks.

At this moment, Ruan Mingyan's voice abruptly rang out: "Is your appetite poor?"

His gaze landed on the virtually untouched food before Yuan Qiao. His tone made it impossible to tell whether it was out of concern or a casual question, while his fingertips unconsciously stroked the table.

Yuan Qiao's movements paused, and she then gently placed her silver chopsticks on the white porcelain chopstick rest, lowering her gaze to warmly reply, "Thank you for Your Highness's concern. Perhaps it was because I stood a bit too long while learning etiquette this morning that I feel somewhat fatigued; it's nothing serious."

Qingdai, standing to the side, did not dare to interrupt, but anxiously clenched her sleeves. With her mistress speaking so lightly, wasn't sheletting down His Highness's rare concern? Jiang Qiyun had bullied people so badly this morning, why didn't Madam seize the opportunity to pour her grievances out?

Ruan Mingyan's gaze swept over the untouched bowl of fresh bamboo shoot and old duck soup before her, and he raised a hand to signal the dining eunuch to step forward. "Remove these greasy items. Bring something lighter."

He added, "Since you are fatigued, you should eat more so your body can hold up."

Hearing this, Qingdai was immediately happy for her mistress; the Crown Prince cared so much, which showed that he still held Madam in his heart.

Seeing a dining eunuch bring over a bowl of lotus seed and lily soup, she quickly ladled a small bowl and presented it to Yuan Qiao.

Yuan Qiao was somewhat uncertain of Ruan Mingyan's intentions.

In this life, she looked forward to Ruan Mingyan's favor, as that was the only way she could gain a firm foothold in the estate. Yet when such care truly fell upon her, she inevitably grew somewhat suspicious, treading every step as if on thin ice and feeling utterly unsettled.

"Thank you, Your Highness, for your consideration." Yuan Qiao thanked him according to ritual, her voice slightly light, wearing an appropriate and delicate smile on her face.

The lotus seed and lily soup was boiled to a sweet, soft, and glutinous texture, just right for swallowing, so Yuan Qiao took small sips of it.

Ruan Mingyan suddenly asked again, "How are your etiquette lessons going?"

Yuan Qiao's heart skipped a beat.

Here it comes.

She raised her eyes, meeting Ruan Mingyan's seemingly calm and rippleless gaze. Deep within those eyes lay a trace of probing that was extremely difficult to detect.

Yuan Qiao steadied her mind, put down the porcelain spoon, and slightly nodded: "The training matron is instructing me painstakingly, and this concubine does not dare to slack off. It's just that I am shallow in my initial learning and still have many inadequacies." Her answer was airtight, respectful, and thorough.

Ruan Mingyan watched her lowered brows and submissive appearance, tapping his fingertips twice on the table. It produced an almost imperceptible faint sound, yet carried a vague intimidation, as if striking the strings of Yuan Qiao's heart.

Yuan Qiao couldn't help pondering: Could it be that his coming here today was specifically to rap her over the knuckles because of Jiang Qiyun being punished in the morning?

She had merely overshadowed Jiang Qiyun while learning etiquette; besides, weren't those hardships brought upon herself by Jiang Qiyun? The training matron had issued the punishment, could that possibly be blamed on her?

A trace of bitterness quietly crept into her heart, but she quickly suppressed it, not daring to show the slightest bit of it, and only buried her head lower.

Seeing Yuan Qiao lowering her brows and looking submissive and resigned, Ruan Mingyan inexplicably felt a surge of irritation; he was sitting right here, yet she refused to show even a shred of grievance? Even when he gave her an out, she didn't know how to go with the flow; she truly was a block of wood.

With such a temperament, if she entered the palace in the future, wouldn't she be eaten down to the bones without a scrap left?

The meal ended hastily amidst various hidden thoughts.

Ruan Mingyan rose and departed, saying nothing more.

Yuan Qiao respectfully escorted him to the courtyard gate, watching his figure disappear around the corner of the corridor before she slowly relaxed her tense shoulders.

Ruan Mingyan's sudden arrival had caught her off guard, and now he had flicked his sleeves and left, likely displeased in his heart. Having offended him repeatedly, she would probably have to be even more careful and cautious in this estate from now on.

Qingdai didn't understand how things had turned out this way; clearly, everything had been fine at first. Seeing the undeniable fatigue and worry between Yuan Qiao's brows, she could only softly comfort her: "Madam shouldn't overthink it. Perhaps His Highness is busy with court affairs outside, which is why he left in a hurry. Since His Highness came to the Watching Moon Courtyard today, it shows he keeps you in his heart."

Hearing this, Yuan Qiao gently hooked the corners of her lips, though the smile failed to reach her eyes, leaving only a lingering bitterness.

If sticking up for his beloved counted as keeping someone in his heart, then those words were indeed correct.

---

Inside the study, Ruan Mingyan was copying calligraphy.

Ever since lunch, his mood had been consistently poor.

Moshu was attending to the brush and ink at the side, noticing something amiss. After Ruan Mingyan ruined his third sheet of calligraphy, Moshu finally couldn't help speaking up: "His Highness has seemed in low spirits ever since returning from Madam Yuan's place today. Did something happen?"

The brush tip paused, and another blot of ink bloomed on the rice paper.

Ruan Mingyan put down the brush, his tone indifferent, "Just trivial matters."

Yet that trace of irritation in his heart refused to dissipate, an emotion he found somewhat inexplicable even to himself.

As a study companion who had followed Ruan Mingyan for over a decade, Moshu understood him best.

Since childhood, the Crown Prince had disciplined himself strictly according to ritual. After being proclaimed Crown Prince, he acted even more cautiously, his emotions never showing on his face. When had he ever been this unsettled on account of a woman?

Moshu weighed his tone and brought it up as if chatting casually: "When Your Highness originally chose Madam Jiang, it was precisely because of her stunning beauty and willful temperament; she was a fine piece placed right into the Second Prince's hands. Since you already had the best candidate, why bring Madam Yuan into the estate as well?"

Ruan Mingyan crumpled the rice paper into a ball and tossed it into the wastebasket, his expression devoid of emotion, "I merely found her pitiful. For a woman to make a living in a place like a song-and-dance house is ultimately not a long-term plan."

Moshu fell silent for a moment.

With Madam Yuan's cold temperament and low birth, was entering this Crown Prince's mansion truly a good thing for her? I'm afraid the hardships ahead would be even greater than those outside.

Putting these causes and effects together instead gave Moshu a sense of Ruan Mingyan's intentions, but he had to offer a reminder: "Since you chose Madam Jiang, you should play the part thoroughly. If the two concubines in the estate stand as rivals with unclear favor, how can those rumors outside about the 'Crown Prince bewitched by beauty' be made credible?"

He paused, lowering his voice, "Besides, if the Empress Dowager/Empress should notice, Madam Yuan's situation would be hard to predict."

Madam Jiang was a target set up by His Highness, like an autumn grasshopper that couldn't leap for long; the Empress probably wouldn't pay her mind for the moment.

Madam Yuan was different, however.

In case the Empress noticed His Highness's true intentions, she probably wouldn't meet a good end.

"You worry too much."

Ruan Mingyan clearly did not wish to discuss it further, turning to ask instead, "Has any movement come from the south?"

Moshu's expression turned stern, casting aside his previous laxity as he respectfully reported, "The Second Prince has been in frequent contact with that person recently; I expect he will make a move soon."

Ruan Mingyan said with ambiguous meaning, "Then add a bit more fuel to the fire."

chapters.title: Provocation
chapters.content:
Ever since that day, Ruan Mingyan never came again, spending several consecutive nights staying at the Listening Wind Courtyard. The servants in the estate were best at flattering the high and stepping on the low; though they dared not do it too blatantly, they nevertheless prioritized everything regarding the Listening Wind Courtyard.

The anxiety that Qingdai had held back for days gathered between her brows, while Yuan Qiao merely leaned against the low couch by the window, gazing blankly at the weeping crabapples in the courtyard.

This year was a warm spring, and right now the crabapples were in full bloom. Clusters of rouge-colored petals hung low, trembling gently in the evening breeze, looking like a bashful beauty lowering her head, or perhaps a silent sigh.

Pity that the crabapples had no fragrance.

While filling Yuan Qiao's cup with tea, Qingdai complained, "His Highness stayed at the Listening Wind Courtyard again tonight. He hasn't even stepped foot over here even once."

She was young after all, and unable to sit still at the slightest hint of disturbance.

Yuan Qiao took a sip of tea and said softly, "Didn't he come twice?"

"How can that be the same?" Qingdai couldn't help stamping her foot. "If Madam Jiang conceives an heir first and claims the advantage of 'eldest,' this estate will belong to her world in the future! By then, even when the Crown Princess enters the estate, His Highness will still remember his affection for her, and your status..."

"Silence!"

Seeing her becoming increasingly unruly with her words, Yuan Qiao chided sharply, slamming her teacup heavily onto the low table so that the warm tea splashed a patch of water stains.

Startled, Qingdai hurriedly clamped her mouth shut, used a handkerchief to wipe Yuan Qiao's hands, and lowered her head to tidy the table.

Yuan Qiao looked at her and asked an irrelevant question, "How long have you been in the estate?"

Although somewhat baffled, Qingdai answered honestly, "This servant was selected into the estate by Mama Jing the year before last. There were several who entered at the same time, and Peilan from the Listening Wind Courtyard was one of them."

She was not a hereditary bondservant born in the household, nor had she signed a life-long indenture; she had been forced to become a servant simply because her family was struggling to get by. Having drifted through several employers at a young age, she naturally cultivated a rather scheming temperament.

Yuan Qiao stared fixedly at her, her gaze deep and heavy, yet she remained silent.

Feeling her heart tremble under that gaze, Qingdai abruptly dropped to her knees and kowtowed in succession to confess her fault.

"Madam, it was this servant who spoke recklessly! Please punish me, Madam!"

"You've been in the estate for two years, where have all your lessons on decorum gone? You can't even tell what should be said and what shouldn't?"

Yuan Qiao's tone was not heavy, but every word pierced like a needle into Qingdai's heart, leaving her barely able to breathe. "You dare to recklessly discuss your superiors behind their backs? Do you no longer want this life of yours? This is the Crown Prince's Mansion; if we were in the palace, not only would your petty life be forfeit, but even I would be implicated by you."

Qingdai had originally thought Yuan Qiao was easy to get along with, but she never expected that when angered, without any harshness or fierce expression, she was even more terrifying than Mama Jing. Her face turned pale with fright, and she begged for mercy repeatedly, "Madam, this servant knows her wrong! This servant will never dare again! In the future, I will definitely keep Madam's teachings in mind, please spare this servant just this once!"

Serving by Yuan Qiao's side was still better than doing coarse and tiring labor. Moreover, Yuan Qiao didn't frequently order her around on ordinary days; compared to the bitter days of the past, this was already countless times better. If she were driven out of the estate, she feared she would no longer have any good place to go.

Yuan Qiao raised a hand to stop her movements and said, "I will spare you for today. If you transgress again in the future, you will be handed over to Mama Jing for disposal; there is no room for you here."

Hearing this, Qingdai nodded repeatedly and hurriedly served Yuan Qiao to rest.

?

The next day during etiquette lessons, Jiang Qiyun was late by another half-hour.

Lately, she had grown increasingly lax with endless excuses. One moment she was feeling unwell, the next she needed to seek His Highness; her etiquette lessons were also learned in a complete mess, perfunctory to the extreme.

Today was especially so. Before she even arrived, her voice had preceded her.

"Serving His Highness was exhausting last night, so I arrived a bit late. Mama, please don't blame me."

As her voice faded, she finally entered the room with a leisurely lotus-step.

Yet her makeup was clearly exquisite, and not a trace of fatigue could be seen on her face; instead, there was a hint of smugness, making it blatantly obvious she was spouting nonsense.

Knowing she was going to stir up trouble again, Yuan Qiao quietly stepped back half a step without a sound.

Sure enough, the moment Mama Jing saw her appearance, she immediately interrogated her, "Madam Jiang has been late for days, and today she is once again so devoid of regard for others. Could it be that you completely disregard decorum in your eyes?"

Jiang Qiyun nonchalantly adjusted the pearl hairpin at her temple, paying little heed to Mama Jing's interrogation, and didn't even bother to bow. "His Highness showed pity, which is why he allowed me to rest a moment longer. Could it be that Mama intends to defy His Highness's will as well?"

With those words, her gaze swept lightly over Yuan Qiao, the provocation self-evident.

Was she flaunting the Crown Prince's favor toward her?

Yuan Qiao felt a flash of surprise in her heart, but she wasn't annoyed; she only found it laughable, hoping that when she was summoned into the palace in the future, she could still remain this arrogant.

Having served the Empress for many years, to the point where even imperial concubines in the palace had to grant her a modicum of respect, when had Mama Jing ever suffered such treatment?

"Audacious!"

She immediately shouted coldly, "Uttering such wild nonsense, do you still remember your own status? You are merely a concubine, yet not even half a month after entering the estate, you act so lawless and willful, do you really think there is no one in this estate who can manage you?!"

The instructor mammy's expression was also unsightly, and she sneered, "Madam Jiang puts on quite a grand display of prestige! Setting aside the fact that the two of us were transferred from the palace to serve and do not fall under the jurisdiction of the Crown Prince's Mansion; purely in terms of rank, Madam Jiang is still below us. How dare you be so rude?"

"Oh, and so what if I am?"

Jiang Qiyun's red lips curved up slightly in a "what can you do to me" posture. "This is the Crown Prince's Mansion. Whomever His Highness favors is the one qualified to speak. Even if the two of you are dissatisfied, what can you do about it?"

!　　"Good, good, good!" The instructor mammy laughed out of extreme anger, repeating the word 'good' three times. "This servant will go straight into the palace to report this to Her Majesty the Empress! Let's hope that before Her Majesty, Madam can still be so glib!"

Angered to the extreme, the instructor mammy stormed off in a rage, flicking her sleeves. Judging by that stance, she would likely go straight into the palace. Mama Jing glanced at Jiang Qiyun and departed with an equally gloomy expression.

Yuan Qiao stood in place, frowning slightly.

In her past life, although Jiang Qiyun had been arrogant, it was merely petty mischief that displeased Mama Jing, which eventually caught the Empress's attention and led to her being summoned into the palace for a reprimand.

Why did Jiang Qiyun dare to be so brazen this time? It seemed as though she was deliberately afraid Her Majesty the Empress wouldn't notice her.

As she was pondering, Jiang Qiyun had already spotted her and sneered, "Some people, even if they stand here, are just like clay idols or wooden puppets, mere ornaments."

With that, without waiting for Yuan Qiao's response, she swept away loftily.

Both startled and angered, Qingdai lowered her voice and said, "Has this Madam Jiang lost her mind? To actually treat Mama Jing and the instructor mammy like that!"

They were people sent from the palace, after all!

Yuan Qiao remained silent.

Such a simple principle was something even Qingdai could see; how could Jiang Qiyun not understand it?

Having been able to firmly sit as the top courtesan of the singing and dancing troupe for so many years, she was naturally not brainless. How could she commit such an act of self-destruction that ruined her own future and needlessly brought disaster upon herself?

What was the purpose of such a deliberate stunt today?

Yuan Qiao's heart grew cold as she suddenly realized she had seemingly underestimated Jiang Qiyun.

She had previously regarded Jiang Qiyun as someone who rose to power purely on looks and flattery; but looking at it now, beneath this swaggering and domineering exterior probably lay a scheme she had never caught a glimpse of.

On the contrary, it was herself who, having never peered into the truth behind this, and having been swayed by chaotic emotions in her past life, had her eyes and heart blinded after her rebirth, only now seeing clearly the situation she was in.

Mama Jing and the instructor mammy had both been driven away in anger, so naturally, there was no need to study etiquette today.

The two of them returned to the courtyard. Yuan Qiao still felt that everything about the matter was fishy, and the sense of unease in her heart refused to subside.

"Qingdai, find a way to go and inquire if any special rumors have spread from the front courtyard recently, especially concerning Madam Jiang. Remember to act with caution and not make a fuss."

Seeing Yuan Qiao's solemn expression, Qingdai knew this matter was no small affair and dared not delay, hastily acknowledging the order and leaving.

Before long, Qingdai hurried back, and the news she brought back made Yuan Qiao's heart violently shake, the Crown Prince had actually bestowed his personal cloud-patterned white jade pendant, which he had carried for years, upon Jiang Qiyun, and even permitted her to enter and exit the study holding the jade pendant.

Such exceptional favor had long since exceeded the bounds of a concubine!

No matter how much Ruan Mingyan favored Jiang Qiyun, he was still the ruler of a generation's crown prince; he couldn't possibly be so muddle-headed as to easily permit her, who had entered the estate just a short time ago, to freely enter and exit the vital area of the study. There was clearly something wrong inside.

And having just obtained a bit of favor, Jiang Qiyun dared to cross swords with Mama Jing, who had the Empress as her backing. If this wasn't done deliberately, Yuan Qiao wouldn't believe it for a second.

What shocked her even more was that, upon careful thought, every promotion of Jiang Qiyun's rank in her past life seemed to have intertwined connections with the Second Prince's faction. And the Second Prince was ultimately stripped of his princely title and exiled to the border precisely because he plotted to harm the Crown Prince and attempted to usurp his position...

Thinking up to this point, combined with Ruan Mingyan's various actions lately, Yuan Qiao realized she seemed to have caught a glimpse of some incredible secret, and instantly felt her heart leap in terror.

The undercurrents in this estate seemed even more turbulent than she had imagined.

chapters.title: Nightmare
chapters.content:
"Madam!"
