Seeing Yuan Qiao stand there in a daze after listening, her fingertips even trembling slightly, Qingdai was startled. "What is wrong with you?"

As she spoke, she half-crouched down, cupped Yuan Qiao's hands in her palms, and gently persuaded, "Is it because His Highness is unusually partial to Madam Jiang that you feel uncomfortable in your heart? You always told this servant not to lose her composure, yet you have lost your own footing instead. The road ahead is still long; who can say what things will look like down the road? Perhaps a turning point will appear, so why torture yourself?"

Yuan Qiao shook her head, her thin lips parting slightly, but in the end she said nothing.

Once those words were uttered aloud, she feared that tonight the two of them would lose their heads.

Seeing that she was reluctant to speak further, Qingdai hurriedly shifted the topic. "Madam, do you think Mama Jing and the others will really go into the palace to report today's events to Her Majesty the Empress?"

"Most likely they will."

Yuan Qiao let out a breath, soothingly patted the back of Qingdai's hand, and spoke in a voice so soft it sounded like a murmur, "Mama Jing has an upright temperament and cannot tolerate any sand in her eyes. Having been by the Empress's side for many years, she is accustomed to being respected. Today, with Jiang Qiyun acting so lawlessly, how could she tolerate it?"

Recalling how Mama Jing and the instructor mammy had looked when enraged, Qingdai still felt lingering fear; but upon a second thought, the one who made a mistake wasn't her own mistress, and a sense of schadenfreude inevitably arose in her heart. She couldn't help gloating, "Won't Madam Jiang be punished this time?"

"Perhaps." Yuan Qiao showed little interest in this.

After all, the methods used in the palace were always tortuous; sometimes a punishment was a reward, and a reward was a punishment. But as long as Ruan Mingyan still needed Jiang Qiyun as a chess piece, her life would never be in danger.

Sure enough, just past noon, Mama Jing returned to the estate with Her Majesty the Empress's imperial edict, summoning Jiang Qiyun into the palace.

Upon learning the news, Yuan Qiao skipped lunch, dismissed even Qingdai, and sat quietly alone in the courtyard for a long time.

After passing through this ordeal, many events of her past life came flooding back. The once-fuzzy memories were now shockingly clear, bit by bit sketching out the hidden chessboard behind the scenes in her mind.

If all the past events had been manipulated by Ruan Mingyan single-handedly, then every humiliation and despair she had suffered, was it not also a gift bestowed by him?

Though she was merely a humble dancing girl, she had a fixed monthly allowance, and sometimes when she was lucky and met generous patrons, she could even earn some tips. Admittedly, such a life could not be considered wealthy, but it was at least carefree and secure; she didn't need to constantly walk on thin ice just to preserve her life, and occasionally when taking leave to return home, she could visit her aunt.

Yet ever since she entered the Crown Prince's Mansion, she never had another night of peaceful sleep, feeling like a fish thrown onto the shore, no matter how she struggled, it only felt like suffocation.

Ruan Mingyan had dragged her into this vortex of power struggle. Knowing what conditions were like inside the estate, he nevertheless looked on coldly, allowing her to suffer every kind of hardship, and even added fuel to the fire behind the scenes, how ruthless!

Furthermore, it was quite possible that when she lost her child back then, his hands had been behind it as well...

Calculating the timeline, it was precisely approaching the juncture where Ruan Mingyan and the Second Prince would completely break faces. Jiang Qiyun was the carefully placed decoy he set up; with the overall situation about to be settled, how could he possibly allow an insignificant concubine like her to disrupt the board?

Moreover, with a humble background like hers, she couldn't even enter the imperial genealogy; what qualification did she have to give birth to the eldest imperial grandson? The Crown Princess had not yet entered the estate; if she were to give birth to an heir first, it would be an immense disrespect to the primary wife.

Her child had come at too inopportune a time and stood in his way, which was why the child could not be kept.

At this train of thought, Yuan Qiao felt a dull, stifling pain in her chest, a dense wave of agony crashing over her like a tide, almost swallowing her whole.

She had once thought that all those past resentments and pains had been worn away during the long, endless nights in the palace. Now, reborn, she could calmly face Ruan Mingyan and Jiang Qiyun, start anew, and slowly walk out a different path.

Yet at this moment, Yuan Qiao realized with utmost clarity that she had never let go at all.

The sun was rising higher, casting brilliant golden light across the courtyard, filtering and scattering down through the crabapple branches. It was warm and cozy, yet Yuan Qiao felt as though she had fallen into an ice cellar, a succession of chills gripping the depths of her heart.

?

Perhaps due to thinking too much during the day, at night Yuan Qiao plunged back into the nightmares of her past life...

It had been overcast for several days, yet not a single drop of rain fell. The horizon was dark and gloomy, as if brewing a terrifying storm, and the thick, heavy moisture made it hard to breathe.

Yuan Qiao was right in the midst of morning sickness, and being disturbed by this weather left her with zero appetite. Only under Qingdai's repeated persuasion did she reluctantly taste a few spoonfuls of pork-bone lotus root soup.

Ever since she became pregnant, she had grown much thinner. All kinds of nourishing delicacies were delivered to the Wangyue Courtyard like a flowing stream, yet she couldn't keep any of it down. The servants gossiped privately behind her back, saying she was a person of thin fortune who couldn't bear such favor.

The imperial physician prescribed formulas, but bowl after bowl of miscarriage-prevention medicine failed to make her feel even a fraction more comfortable; instead, she suffered from insomnia every night, her spirit growing steadily weaker.

Looking listless, Yuan Qiao had the food cleared away and wanted to take a short nap when she suddenly felt a knife-twisting pain in her abdomen, her vision darkened, and she couldn't even stand steadily. Losing her strength all at once, she collapsed beside the low table by the window.

Terrified out of her wits, Qingdai panicked and helped her up, wanting to summon someone to fetch the estate doctor. But looking down, she saw a pool of scarlet red on Yuan Qiao's skirt...

By the time the medical officer arrived, it was already beyond saving.

Jiang Qiyun led people to surround the Wangyue Courtyard, loudly demanding a thorough investigation. Yet in the end, the imperial physician concluded that it was due to Yuan Qiao consuming a chaotic mixture of foods that clashed with her medicine, and even accused her of knowing she was pregnant yet lacking self-restraint, thereby losing the child.

Ever since her morning sickness became severe, she could hardly eat much food to begin with. This accusation was absurd to the extreme, yet no one cared about her defense, nor did anyone pay attention to her shrill, miserable cries.

As the personal maid who attended to her daily diet and living quarters, Qingdai naturally bore unshirkable blame for such an incident happening, and she was immediately sold off.

Those matrons possessed immense strength; before Qingdai could even finish pleading for mercy, her mouth was stuffed and she was dragged away. Yuan Qiao watched as she struggled desperately, shaking her head toward her while unable to make a sound, her tears falling one by one and splashing onto the ground to stain a damp patch.

Jiang Qiyun's gaze fell upon her flat lower abdomen, and she sighed gloomily, "It seems younger sister truly lacks this fortune."

Later, everyone dispersed, the courtyard gates were shut tightly, and no one ever heard her painful, desperate groans again...

The rainstorm that had been brewing for days finally fell, fierce and heavy as if the sky had torn open. The rain was swept by the howling gale through the unclosed window, smashing into the room and leaving it dark, cold, and damp all over.

She lay on the bed, curled up in pain, with no one caring whether she lived or died...

"Madam! Madam!"

Qingdai's anxious voice rang in her ear. Suddenly feeling herself being gently pushed, Yuan Qiao groggily opened her eyes to see Qingdai leaning over her, looking at her with an anxious expression.

"Madam, what is wrong with you? Were you caught in a nightmare?"

Yuan Qiao stared blankly at Qingdai, her hand instinctively touching her lower abdomen; it was completely flat, yet it seemed to retain the twisting pain from the dream.

A warm handkerchief covered her forehead. After a long while, Yuan Qiao gathered her scattered wits and managed to distinguish the dream from reality.

She and Qingdai were both doing well right now, and that unmeant child had not yet arrived.

Yuan Qiao propped herself up into a half-sitting position, raised a hand to gently pinch the soft flesh on Qingdai's cheek, and smiled, "I'm fine, I just had a dream, it's nothing."

Only, that smile didn't reach her eyes, overflowing with bitterness no matter how one looked at it.

"Madam must have dreamed of something frightening."

Allowing herself to be pinched, Qingdai busied herself arranging the soft pillows behind Yuan Qiao's back, then used a handkerchief to carefully wipe the cold sweat from her forehead. Clearly still young herself, she acted as if she had endless worries to bear.

"Madam, don't be afraid. This servant is guarding right outside your room. If you need anything, just call out. Besides, there are estate guards patrolling at night, it's very safe."

Qingdai's soft and gentle voice was like a small hand smoothing away the pain from the dream one by one, clearly and truly telling her that it was only a nightmare and everything was still in time now.

Yuan Qiao's heart felt as though it had been gently bumped by something, turning achingly soft, and she couldn't help nodding, "I know."

Yet, what she feared was never those overt blades and spears; the methods of this inner courtyard were sometimes even more terrifying than swords.

With a "pfft," Qingdai couldn't help laughing out loud. "Madam's expression just now looked just like a little child needing to be coaxed. Go to sleep quickly; if you have no spirit tomorrow, what will we do?"

Outside the window, the chirping of unknown insects rose and fell, and moonlight filtered in through the paper-pasted window, serene and peaceful.

Yuan Qiao lay back down. This time, she dreamed of nothing at all.

chapters.title: The Crown Prince Returns to the Manor
chapters.content:
Ever since Jiang Qiyun was summoned to the palace, Ruan Mingyan had remained there to manage official business, neglecting to return to the estate.

Like the other imperial princes, Ruan Mingyan had originally resided within the palace. Later, as his external assignments gradually increased and traveling in and out of the palace became inconvenient, the Emperor specially bestowed this Crown Prince's Mansion upon him.

Now that neither he nor Jiang Qiyun was in the manor, with the instructor dowager guiding Jiang Qiyun in the palace and Nanny Jing tied up with a myriad of trivial matters, temporarily unable to spare attention for Yuan Qiao; she unexpectedly found herself enjoying a measure of leisure.

To Yuan Qiao, this place had been like a prison in both her past and present lives. Yet today, her frame of mind was quietly changing.

Jiang Qiyun relied on nothing more than her beauty and a degree of scheming to climb step by step from the status of a songstress to a imperial consort of the second rank, all because she was "useful"thus enjoying boundless glory and favor. Why could she not forge a path to survival for herself?

Although undercurrents surged within the manor and human hearts were unfathomable, she had after all lived a lifetime longer than others and possessed the advantage of foreknowledge. If, after repeating this life, she were still to live at the mercy of others and be trampled underfoot, would that not be a joke?

Yuan Qiao knew full well that she could not master the arts of ingratiating herself and currying favor; while Jiang Qiyun’s methods were effective, they were not suited for her. Moreover, her previous notion of "making a long-term plan and moving people with affection" had completely dissipated the moment she realized Ruan Mingyan’s so-called "favor" toward Jiang Qiyun was merely a matter of balance and exploitation.

For a man like Ruan Mingyan, his heart was set on the supreme throne of the nine-fold heavens. To him, romance was likely just another tool to manipulate human hearts. To survive in his hands, let alone live with dignity, the only key was the word "usefulness."

Yuan Qiao sat alone by the window for half the day, dissecting the tangled mess of her circumstances piece by piece. The vague notion in her heart finally crystallized into a clear, cold, and hard resolve.

In this vortex, she would fight for a path to survival for herself. She would never again be at the mercy of others and die an obscure, senseless death.

In her past life, she had been like a drifting flower swept along by the current, utterly lacking in autonomy. Now, she finally saw her position clearly, understood the chessboard before her, and perceived the path ahead.

Yet, before Yuan Qiao could figure out her next move, she suddenly heard that Ruan Mingyan had returned to the manor.

A pang of tightness gripped Yuan Qiao’s heart: How could it be so soon?

In her memory, he should have stayed overnight in the palace for the next few days until Jiang Qiyun was punished and fainted, at which point he would defy the Empress's decree to bring her out of the manor, thereby cementing his reputation for being "drowned in beauty."

Yet now, he had returned after staying in the palace for only a single night... Could some unexpected change have occurred?

Suppressing her unease, she instructed Qingdai to go out and make inquiries.

Before long, Qingdai returned with the news: "His Royal Highness the Crown Prince has indeed returned to the manor, and he has even ordered meals to be served in the flower parlor. Now that Madam Jiang is not here, with only Madam in the manor, this is an opportunity that must not be missed. Would Madam wish to go to the flower parlor... to attend to His Royal Highness during his meal?"

Having learned a lesson, Qingdai’s words lacked their former impatience, carrying instead a measure of deliberation.

Though Yuan Qiao had yet to figure out the reason behind this, she understood that if she remained confined to her corner forever, she would never have a chance to turn her fortunes around.

This time, she must fight.

For the foolish self of her past life, and for the child who had never been born into this world.

Given Ruan Mingyan’s temperament, if she proactively showed goodwill, he likely would not drive her away; at worst, she would merely receive a cold face. Having swallowed so much bitterness before, what did this bit of grievance amount to?

Thus, smoothing her robes and rising, she led Qingdai toward the flower parlor with the resolve of one marching to their death. It was clearly just a meal, yet it felt like heading to a battlefield.

---

In truth, Ruan Mingyan had originally intended to play his part to the end, remaining in the palace to bide his time until the moment was right, thereby adding another stroke to his reputation for "indulging in beauty" and fully executing the act of losing his sense of proportion out of favoritism for Jiang Qiyun.

Once the bait was cast, the restless fish would naturally begin to flounder.

Without exerting much effort, he could haul in a massive net.

Yet, as luck would have it, the confidant left behind in the manor reported that ever since Jiang Qiyun was summoned to the palace, Yuan Qiao had remained secluded behind closed doors, frequently sitting alone in a daze and experiencing nightmares at night.

For some reason, after reading the pigeon-delivered message, a faint sense of unease had lingered in Ruan Mingyan’s heart.

He was not a man mired in romance; keeping himself strictly disciplined for all these years, he did not even have a maidservant close at hand to attend to him. Even Jiang Qiyun, his nominal favorite concubine, had been told upon their first meeting that it was merely a transaction, and the so-called bed-chamber services were entirely Jiang Qiyun's one-man show.

Yet Yuan Qiao was different.

She was timid as a rabbit, had not been in the manor for long, and had no one to rely on. Having gone through this ordeal, she must surely be terrified.

After all, she was someone he had personally chosen to bring into the manor; he could not completely ignore her.

Thus, the usually composed, steady, and unflappable Crown Prince learned for the very first time in his life what it meant to yearn for someone.

Until today, when another express letter arrived stating that Yuan Qiao had once again sat in solitude for half a day with a desolate expression, Ruan Mingyan could finally hold back no longer and resolved to return to the manor to take a look.

He thought to himself: Just a single look would suffice.

Once he smoothed away that inexplicable agitation in his heart and figured out why this sentiment had arisen, everything would naturally return to its proper course.

Hurrying back to the manor, Ruan Mingyan immediately ordered meals to be set and sent Moshu in person to summon her.

Moshu had never seen his master exhibit such sharp and stern tones; daring not to speak further, he accepted the order and departed.

Lowering his head to glance at his solemn, rigid court robes, Ruan Mingyan suddenly recalled the panicked expression Yuan Qiao wore when she first met him. Fearing this attire might make her uncomfortable once more, he paused, suppressed that trace of latent urgency, and turned back to his bedchamber to change first.

He would change into light-colored casual attire... perhaps that would appear somewhat gentler.

---

In the flower parlor, when Yuan Qiao arrived, the servants were methodically arranging the dining table, but Ruan Mingyan was nowhere to be seen.

Yuan Qiao simply instructed directly: "Set another place."

With Jiang Qiyun away under punishment, Yuan Qiao could naturally assert a degree of authority within the manor. Daring not to be negligent, the servants hastily added a setting, carefully placing it beside the principal seat.

When Ruan Mingyan walked into the flower parlor after changing his clothes, he saw Yuan Qiao rolling up her sleeves and holding chopsticks, serving food onto his plate. Sweeping his gaze around, however, he failed to see Moshu, causing his brow to furrow slightly.

Raising her eyes at that exact moment and noticing his displeasure, Yuan Qiao quickly set down her chopsticks and bowed in salute.

She hid her emotions impeccably; her voice was soft, cautious, and slightly trembling at the tail end. To anyone watching, she appeared merely as a timid woman clumsily and carefully trying to please.

"Please forgive me, Your Highness. This concubine heard that Your Highness had returned to the manor and presumptuously came... to attend to Your Highness's meal."

Lowering his gaze, Ruan Mingyan quietly observed her for a moment.

He had never understood why she was so afraid of him. Every time they met, she looked like a startled bird, yet he had never once displayed a harsh expression before her.

The famously virtuous Crown Prince washed his hands, silently took his seat, and mused to himself: Could it be that he was usually too stern and possessed a fearsome reputation, causing her to be this terrified of him?

Seeing that Ruan Mingyan offered no rebuke, Yuan Qiao secretly breathed a sigh of relief, knowing she had managed to muddle through. Relying on her memory of his few sparse preferences, she placed a few more dishes into an empty bowl on the side. Only after the food-tasting eunuch inspected them did she serve them to Ruan Mingyan.

Most of these were light, seasonal dishes. For now, only cold appetizers and small side dishes had been served, along with staple foods of peach-blossom polished rice porridge and tribute rice, some preserved fruits and candied treats; the heavier main courses had yet to be brought out.

Ruan Mingyan’s gaze involuntarily fell upon the hands holding the chopsticks.

Slender, delicate fingers, white and glowing like jade; because she exerted slight force, the fingertips revealed a faint blush, and her nails were tinted with a light cherry-colored koudan, refined and unique. From beneath her rolled-up cuffs, a section of snowy wrist resembled jade, and the lotus silver bracelet on her wrist swayed gently with her movements, casting a delicate, shifting luster.

For a moment, it made one unable to look away.

It was not until Yuan Qiao set down her chopsticks and offered the white porcelain bowl filled with porridge before him that he snapped back to his senses.

In the white jade porcelain bowl, the thick, smooth rice porridge had been dyed a pale pink by peach blossom petals, garnished on top with a few fresh petals, appealing in color, aroma, and taste.

Another plate held accompanying side dishes: crisp mixed spring radishes, cold-dressed malantou greens, a pair of chopsticks holding tender spring Chinese chives, and half a small dish of braised pork with spring bamboo shoots.

She must have deliberately inquired about his preferences to arrange a meal so pleasing to his heart.

His fingertips unconsciously rubbed together, suppressing the ripples rising in his heart, while his voice remained steady: "Sit down and eat together. Let the servants attend us."

"Yes, Your Highness."

Obediently complying, Yuan Qiao set aside the jade chopsticks and small plates used for serving food and took her seat.

At this moment, Moshu, who had rushed to the Watching Moon Courtyard only to find it empty, returned in a hurry to report. As his gaze swept over Yuan Qiao seated beside Ruan Mingyan, the words of apology hovering in his throat made a half-turn and were silently swallowed back. Lowering his head, he stood aside to wait.

Seeing that Ruan Mingyan had not touched his food, Yuan Qiao tilted her head slightly to look at him, her voice soft and carrying a timid, ingratiating tone: "Your Highness, what is the matter? Is the food not to your liking?"

"Nothing."

Ruan Mingyan’s glance swept past Moshu. Picking up his chopsticks, he tasted a piece of the crisp mixed spring radishes; the seasoning was precisely balanced, the shredded radish crisp, tender, fresh, and sweet, carrying a slight salty-spicy kick that was remarkably appetizing.

"The taste is quite good. You should try some as well."

"Yes." Her heart easing slightly, Yuan Qiao began to eat.

chapters.title: Attending to the Brush and Ink
chapters.content:
Yet, with matters heavily weighing on her mind, Yuan Qiao had no heart for the meal and ate only a little.

Ruan Mingyan, on the other hand, had a good appetite. He finished the dishes Yuan Qiao had served him earlier, and after the main courses were served, he consumed an additional bowl of Zhuxi tribute rice before finally setting down his chopsticks.

Seeing that he had finished his meal, Yuan Qiao softly instructed the servants to clear the table.

The flower parlor quieted down, and a pot of clear tea accompanied by several exquisite pastries and tea-pairing preserved fruits was promptly presented.

Yuan Qiao poured a cup of tea and handed it to Ruan Mingyan, then poured one for herself. Her gaze brushed over a plate of osmanthus cakes, and for some reason, she recalled the awkward moment she had choked while eating pastries on that day, causing her to subtly shift her gaze away.

Whether intentional or not, Ruan Mingyan pushed that very plate of osmanthus cakes toward her direction. "You appear somewhat thinner. Is the food in the manor not to your liking?"

Yuan Qiao quickly replied in a soft voice: "Thank Your Highness for your concern; this concubine ordinarily eats very little."

As she secretly deliberated whether she should find a topic to probe into the matter of Jiang Qiyun, she grew fearful that doing so would seem too deliberate and let Ruan Mingyan perceive something amiss. While she hesitated, she heard him speak first.

"Madam Jiang’s affair has nothing to do with you; do not distress yourself over it."

The Crown Prince rubbed the rim of his teacup with his fingertips, his tone casual and voice clear, carrying a detached, superior composure, as if he could effortlessly see through her hesitation and worry.

The white porcelain cup held pale green tea, gripped by his well-articulated hand. The tea rippled slightly as it was held, sending up curling wisps of fragrance.

The remark was tossed off lightly, as though merely mentioned in passing. Without waiting for her response, he continued: "Have you grown accustomed to everything since entering the manor? If there is any shortage, simply speak to Nanny Jing."

Pretending not to have heard the previous sentence, Yuan Qiao obediently answered: "Everything in the manor is fine. Nanny Jing has arranged all matters quite properly, so Your Highness may rest easy."

Hearing this, Ruan Mingyan tightened his grip on the teacup, pale blue veins silently straining across the back of his hand, while the corners of his lips rose in an imperceptible arc.

Had he not known that Yuan Qiao was tormented day and night in the manor with unease, he might truly have been fooled by her.

She was clearly as timid as a mouse, rushing out to seek comfort the moment she heard he had returned like a helpless little cat. Yet when he actually sat by her side, she only looked at him timidly, refusing to utter a single word even when he patiently questioned her over and over.

So contrary, yet precisely because of that, so endearing that he could not set his mind at ease regarding her.

Seeing Ruan Mingyan merely toying with his teacup, Yuan Qiao could not help feeling a degree of doubt. There was nothing particularly special about that white porcelain cup... Could it be that she had said something wrong?

Though their thoughts twisted through a hundred turns, neither revealed a thing.

Watching anxiously as the budding conversation turned cold once more, Qingdai inwardly fretted, hoping her mistress would voice her grievances and act coquettishly toward the Crown Prince. Yet, not daring to act presumptuously before her superiors, she twisted her embroidered handkerchief until it was nearly shredded.

With Second Prince Ruan Mingcheng making frequent moves in He County, the net was about to be drawn shut. To avoid any flaws, Ruan Mingyan dared not relax; many matters required his personal supervision to set his mind at ease, leaving him with little leisure time.

After finishing his tea, he stood up, smoothed his robes, and prepared to head to the study. His gaze swept over Yuan Qiao, who was clearly distracted yet putting up a brave front, and after a moment of hesitation, he spoke: "I still have important matters awaiting attention. If you have nothing else to do, come and attend to the brush and ink."

Was this permission for her to enter the study?

Such an exceptional privilege would be nothing special for the heavily favored Jiang Qiyun, but bestowed upon her, it was truly astonishing.

Was he testing her, or seeing how obedient she was, planning to use her as a pawn as well?

Yuan Qiao instinctively lifted her face to look at Ruan Mingyan, who was already preparing to stride toward the study, and happened to catch his gaze, which was as cold as a deep pool. Realizing her lack of composure, she quickly lowered her eyes, assumed a fitting look of timidity, and spoke in a nervous tone: "Your Highness, this concubine knows her status is humble. Would it be inappropriate for her to enter a restricted place like the study? Nanny Jing instructed me to thoroughly memorize the rules of the manor, and this concubine dares not overstep."

Let alone Yuan Qiao’s shock, even Moshu, who routinely attended closely upon Ruan Mingyan, was astonished by this arrangement. However, finding it inconvenient to refute Ruan Mingyan’s face before others, he merely glanced at him without a word, standing quietly to the side to wait.

The young woman lowered her head, revealing a section of snowy neck beneath her dark hair, appearing utterly harmless and fragile.

"Rules are dead things." Ruan Mingyan calmly glanced at the hesitant Moshu, his voice flat and even. "I permit your attendance; no one will dare to wag their tongues."

Hearing this, though she could not fathom the reason, Yuan Qiao obediently complied and followed Ruan Mingyan toward the study.

Faced with this sudden arrangement, she was indeed somewhat at a loss. In her past life, she had never possessed the qualifications to set foot in Ruan Mingyan’s study.

With such a change having occurred, did it mean the path ahead was also quietly shifting?

---

Mid-spring brought frequent rains, and gathering banks of dark clouds hung across the sky, leaving one to wonder whether a heavy downpour was brewing.

Yuan Qiao followed Ruan Mingyan through several moon gates to the entrance of the study. The guards on duty pushed open the study doors and bowed in salute to the pair.

Qingdai was left outside.

Entering the study, Yuan Qiao cast a subtle, sweeping glance around.

The interior was furnished with classic elegance. In the center sat a huanghuali wood desk, and hanging on the wall behind it was a Painting of Eight Steeds. The artist’s skill was profound; the eight steeds were lifelike, appearing as though they might leap forth at any moment. Beneath the scroll stood a half-man-high shelf holding various ornaments, while the desk and the low table by the window were embellished with a few pots of verdant bamboo, adding a touch of greenery to the room.

Behind a gauze screen, towering sandalwood shelves were dimly visible, lined with various collections of books and illustrated scrolls.

Seeing Ruan Mingyan stride to the desk, seat himself, and begin reviewing memorials, Yuan Qiao immediately collected her thoughts. Lifting one sleeve with a single hand, she stood a short distance away and began to grind the ink.

A chill agarwood burned in the beast-shaped incense burner; thin sunlight pierced the thick clouds, casting a soft glow upon the patterned paper windows. The room was utterly silent, save for the occasional chirping of cicadas outside.

The bright cinnabar-red tribute ink gradually dissolved on the snowy Duan inkstone, blooming into a striking, vivid crimson.

Ruan Mingyan raised his eyes to look at Yuan Qiao. Slightly surprised by her skilled movements, he asked: "Have you read some books before?"

Yuan Qiao started, feeling as though the tribute cinnabar inkstick, carved with rolling cloud patterns in her hand, had suddenly grown scalding hot, nearly causing her to lose her grip.

A belated chill crept up her spine. Noticing Ruan Mingyan beginning to process state affairs, she had instinctively selected this tribute cinnabar inkstick from among the many ink blocks on the wooden shelf, along with the white Duan inkstone best suited for grinding cinnabar.

In that instant, she had forgotten that these were skills she had learned from the head-nannies only after entering the palace in her past life. At the present moment, she ought to have been entirely ignorant of such things. Ruan Mingyan might have summoned her merely to put on a show rather than genuinely requiring her attendance; she had not expected to be so careless.

Suppressing her momentary panic, Yuan Qiao lowered her voice and said: "I merely learned a superficial smattering of it from the older sisters back in the quarter; it is not worth mentioning."

At that, Ruan Mingyan’s gaze naturally fell upon the brightly colored crimson ink pooled in the white Duan inkstone, a trace of faint probing flashing through his eyes.

For the finest cinnabar ink, ink ground on a white Duan inkstone yielded a purer, more vivid color, making it ideal for imperial red-ink annotations; furthermore, once the ink settled, its consistency remained even and smooth, making strokes full and lustrous. With a casual pick, she had selected his most frequently used imperial snow inkstone, and even the red ink was a tribute item exclusively supplied to the royal family, showing she possessed a discerning eye.

Though song-and-dance quarters occasionally housed courtesans skilled in calligraphy and ink-grinding, most possessed shallow skills and rarely came into contact with such imperial tribute items. How could she display such unique discernment?

Clearly knowledgeable yet deliberately concealing it, was she feigning ignorance... or intentionally hiding something?

chapters.title: Books Are Better Than Him?
chapters.content:
Seeing that Yuan Qiao was being vague, Ruan Mingyan temporarily put aside his lingering doubts, raised a hand to open a memorial, and said, "You needn't wait upon me constantly. The number three shelf in the Bing section mostly holds travelogues and amusing anecdotes. If you find it dull, help yourself and read whatever you like."

With that, he casually waved a hand toward the bookshelves, then turned his head to speak in low tones with Moshu.

Knowing that Ruan Mingyan had serious matters to discuss and was using this pretext to dismiss her, Yuan Qiao obediently complied. She stepped past the gauze curtain embroidered with bamboo and rock patterns and entered the inner chamber.

The inner room was partitioned off by a carved screen. Near the window at the front stood a daybed for resting, while the back was lined with tall bookshelves. Although they held a vast collection of texts, the space did not feel heavy or stale with the smell of antiquity; instead, it was suffused with a faint, elegant fragrance.

Following the serial numbers carved into the shelves, Yuan Qiao searched until she found that the scrolls and picture books were all neatly arranged and completely free of dust. Among them were no few rare and unique editions.

Her gaze swept across them one by one, then suddenly halted. On one of the shelves sat a complete set of The Records of Zuo's Observations and Hearings. The spines were crisp and sturdy, wrapped in cloth sleeves and appearing exceedingly well-preserved.

The first six volumes of this book largely recorded dynastic institutions and systems, while the final four recorded historical sites, miscellaneous essays, and official anecdotes. Its writing style was unconstrained and brimming with whimsical delight; during her lonely years in the deep palace in her past life, it had been one of her few sources of comfort.

Yuan Qiao reached out to take the first volume, carefully unwrapped the fine silk book cover, and flipped through it briefly. The pages were slightly yellowed, carrying a faint scent of sweet-clover herb. Confirming it was the exact edition she had read before, she clutched the book, sat down by the low table near the window, and quietly began to read.

She had never been a studious person in the past, nor had she ever been given the opportunity. It was not until she entered the palace and, through a twist of fate, acquired a head maid who was well-read in poetry and history, that many things changed thereafter.

Because of a transgression, that woman was demoted to serve in the Cold Palace. After greasing some palms, she was assigned to serve in Yuan Qiao's remote quarters. Palace days were long; when the maid had leisure, she would teach Yuan Qiao a bit of calligraphy and painting. Yuan Qiao gradually developed a taste for it, often following along to read, and no longer found the days difficult to endure.

This set of The Records of Zuo's Observations and Hearings had been her favorite back then.

A breeze stirred outside, scattering the clouds so that the warm sunlight poured through the lattice windows, casting a glow upon her body and driving away the lingering chill of spring.

Yuan Qiao gradually became absorbed in her reading, feeling as though she had drifted back to those quiet, lonely days in the palace, momentarily forgetting where she was.

Having finished giving instructions to Moshu, Ruan Mingyan wondered why she had gone so quiet. The moment he raised his eyes, he saw her sitting alone by the window, holding a volume of a book and reading with intense concentration. She seemed to have reached a particularly amusing part, as a gentle, subtle smile curved her brows and eyes, making it impossible to look away.

Today she was simply adorned; her waterfall-like dark hair was half-coiled with a jade hairpin, while the rest hung loosely over her shoulders. A light green dress fittingly outlined her slender silhouette. At this moment, enveloped by the hazy halo of light from outside the window, she possessed a quiet, peaceful stillness that seemed untouched by time.

Seeing her so engrossed, Ruan Mingyan refrained from disturbing her. The two of them simply stayed like this in the study, each busy with their own tasks. The sunlight outside was bright and fine, while the interior was tranquil, a harmonious scene indeed.

As evening approached, the kitchens sent someone to inquire whether dinner should be served in the floral hall.

Hearing this, Yuan Qiao looked up and was startled to realize that it was already quite late; thick clouds rolled across the horizon, and the sun was setting behind the western hills.

"Your Highness."

Belatedly remembering that she was supposed to be serving Ruan Mingyan, yet having completely forgotten due to her deep absorption in reading, she hurriedly set down the book, rose, walked to his side, and said softly, "It is getting late. Though official business is pressing, Your Highness must still care for your health and not overwork yourself. Shall we have dinner first?"

Ruan Mingyan closed the memorial in his hand. The documents previously piled on his desk had mostly been reviewed; earlier, he had already had Moshu take them away.

He tilted his head to look at Yuan Qiao. His gaze was slightly dark, carrying a faint emotion that Yuan Qiao found unfamiliar. He seemed as though he wanted to say something, but ultimately held his tongue. After laying down his brush, he granted the request of the kitchen servant.

Ruan Mingyan rose to wash his hands and stepped outward, only to notice that Yuan Qiao was not following. "What is it?"

Yuan Qiao had originally been somewhat surprised that Ruan Mingyan was listening to advice so easily. Seeing him ask, she pointed toward the book on the low table and tentatively asked, "Your Highness, would you permit this concubine to take this book back to her courtyard? Once I finish reading it, I shall return it."

Ruan Mingyan's gaze swept over the book. She hadn't even flipped through many pages all afternoon; she had truly been reading it carefully.

Could it genuinely be that interesting?

He had labored over official documents in this study the entire afternoon, yet she had paid him not a whit of attention. Forget about providing the companion of a clever beauty or pouring tea and water; not a single glance had fallen upon him.

Weren't you afraid to the point of losing sleep every night? Now that the opportunity is right before you, why aren't you cherishing it at all?

Ruan Mingyan let out an almost imperceptible low hum, his voice slightly cool. "This is a rare and unique edition. How can you just take it away at will?"

Seeing Ruan Mingyan's attitude, Yuan Qiao pressed her lips together, knowing she had overstepped. He had allowed her into the study in the first place merely to set up a new target; she had foolishly let delusions grow, imagining he would show her a degree of leniency.

Yuan Qiao hurriedly curtsied and said, "It was presumptuous of me. Finding this book quite fascinating after reading a portion, I grew bold enough to borrow it from Your Highness. I hope Your Highness is not displeased."

Lowering his gaze to her cautious and timid appearance, Ruan Mingyan sighed, and the slight annoyance in his heart abruptly dissipated.

Fine.

Why was he getting worked up over her?

With such a cowardly temperament, a slightly darkened face scared her into this state, what other ulterior motives could she possibly harbor? What she said just now might have taken her a long time of repeating silently in her heart before she dared to speak. In this vast Crown Prince's Mansion, the only person she could rely on was him. If even he treated her coldly...

"If you have free time, come back and read tomorrow." His tone finally softened.

Did this mean... he was allowing her to come to the study tomorrow?

Had Ruan Mingyan always been such an easy person to get along with? Or had he made up his mind to elevate her as well, putting on a joint act alongside Jiang Qiyun?

Come to think of it, the drama of concubines fighting for favor and a chaotic inner courtyard was far more believable than the Crown Prince suddenly becoming infatuated with a singing- troupe headliner.

Hiding her thoughts deep within, Yuan Qiao lifted her head, assuming an expression of pure innocence and docility. "Does Your Highness mean... this concubine may come here again tomorrow?"

Meeting Yuan Qiao's gaze, which held a mixture of surprise and hope, Ruan Mingyan raised an eyebrow slightly. "What, you're unwilling?"

"Naturally I am willing. Thank Your Highness for this grace." Yuan Qiao hastily stood up, her brows curving into a bright, genuine smile. This smile was clear and radiant, devoid of any ingratiating intent, making anyone who saw it feel their spirits lift in kind.

Why was she so easily coaxed?

"Let's go." Suppressing the urge to reach out and ruffle her hair, Ruan Mingyan averted his gaze and stepped toward the floral hall.

Yuan Qiao nodded gently.

Whether it was utilization or an act, no matter what his purpose was, this was a good thing for her.

In the eyes of the servants, for her to receive such special favor meant she was favored. In the future, those covert slights and evaluations would have to be reined in somewhat.

Even Jiang Qiyun, who was accustomed to throwing her weight around in the residence, would likely have to weigh things carefully when the time came.

However, if she truly formed a pincer formation with Jiang Qiyun, it would probably become even harder to stay clear of the treacherous undercurrents of the imperial court. It was hateful that in her past life she had been confined to the square inch of the inner courtyard, struggling even to preserve her life, and knew pitifully little about the grand affairs of the outer court. Right now, she had virtually no foresight to lean upon.

Yuan Qiao sighed inwardly as she followed Ruan Mingyan's footsteps.

Today, Ruan Mingyan was wearing pale green casual robes, the collar and cuffs embroidered with elegant scroll-grass patterns in silver thread. The heavy dignity of the imperial court was put away, making him look like a noble scion of an illustrious clan, graceful and lofty.

After the initial shock immediately following her rebirth, she no longer felt such intense fear toward Ruan Mingyan. However, the resentment and pain deep in her heart, nurtured by the blood and tears of her past life, constantly reminded her never to repeat the same mistakes.

Entering the floral hall, the dining table had already been set. Yuan Qiao noticed that the servants' gazes toward her carried an extra measure of reverence, which she found utterly ridiculous.

Such was the way of the world, yet it also proved that what she was doing right now was correct.

Since Yuan Qiao had made up her mind to vie for favor, and her approach needed to be different from Jiang Qiyun's, being gentle and attentive suited her best. After all, she had no family background to rely on; she could only establish her footing through Ruan Mingyan's scraps of favor.

Rousing her spirits, she served him with increasing meticulousness and care, making even the attending eunuchs feel somewhat inadequate by comparison.

"Your Highness, please try this Green Stream Soup as well."

With all sorts of matters pressing down on him, Ruan Mingyan had originally lacked much appetite. Yet seeing Yuan Qiao gazing at him with eager eyes, purely hoping he would eat a bit more, for some reason, the words of polite refusal died on his lips and could not be spoken.

Fine, he would taste some, if only not to dash her good intentions.

She likely realized she had been somewhat inattentive during the day, and having been frightened by him earlier, was now racking her brains to make up for it. If he refused again, who knew if she would be able to sleep peacefully tonight?

Ruan Mingyan reluctantly finished more than half a bowl of the soup. Seeing Yuan Qiao reach out to ladle him more, he gave a light sigh. "Sit down and eat with me."

"Understood." Yuan Qiao stopped what she was doing and sat down as told.
